docs.title: The factory API
docs.text:
Summary

The Bellman factory is fourteen public functions of the package bellman, which act on two dictionaries of one shape and on one stage class. Three read files into a record or into the syntactic trellis, the model as written, two elaborate, three bind, one appends a period, one elaborates and binds a syntactic trellis in one call, one runs the whole route, two draw and one counts what a verb changed. This page lists them, with the page that states each one's signature, what it reads, what it returns and what it refuses; The Bellman factory is the route through them on the durables model.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — The Bellman factory: the route and the words; The stage: the stage that elaboration returns. Used by — Stage functions, Recipe functions, Period functions and The trellis factory: the four reference pages. See also — Model directory layout: the folders of a registry.

docs.title: 1 The fourteen functions
docs.text:
A function of a stage is imported from bellman.stage, one of a period from bellman.period and one of a trellis from bellman.trellis, as from bellman.trellis import load_recipe; the refusal class FactoryError from bellman.refusals.

Function Returns Reference bellman.stage.load_stage(path) the record of one stage file Stage functions §2 bellman.stage.elaborate_stage(record, bind=True) the stage of a record, with the sources it supplies bound Stage functions §2 bellman.trellis.load_recipe(directory, recipe, **fills) the syntactic trellis of a registry Recipe functions §2 bellman.trellis.assemble_trellis(directory, recipe, **fills) the specified trellis of a registry Recipe functions §4 bellman.trellis.accrete(trellis, period, inter_connector=None) the trellis with the period appended Period functions §3 bellman.period.diagram_period(trellis, h) a drawing of one period Period functions §5 bellman.trellis.load_trellis(file) the syntactic trellis of a trellis file The trellis factory §2 bellman.trellis.elaborate_trellis(syntactic, previous=None) the elaborated trellis, symbolic The trellis factory §3 bellman.trellis.calibrate_trellis(elaborated, syntactic) a new elaborated trellis, its stages calibrated The trellis factory §4 bellman.trellis.methodize_trellis(elaborated, syntactic) a new elaborated trellis, its stages methodized The trellis factory §4 bellman.trellis.configure_trellis(elaborated, syntactic) a new elaborated trellis, its stages configured The trellis factory §4 bellman.trellis.specify_trellis(syntactic, previous=None, kinds=KINDS) the specified trellis of a syntactic trellis, bound under the kinds kinds names among calibration, methods and settings, the three kinds of KINDS, each stage occurrence copied once The trellis factory §4.1 bellman.trellis.respecify_trellis(specified, before, syntactic, kinds=KINDS) the trellis specify_trellis(syntactic) returns, made from the trellis specified for before by binding again the stage occurrences whose record changed The trellis factory §4.2 bellman.trellis.changed_positions(before, after) the positions a verb bound, a copy of a binding among them The trellis factory §5 bellman.trellis.diagram_trellis(trellis, periods=None) a drawing of the periods and their inter-period connectors The trellis factory §6

Five functions of a period are imported beside them, the first four from bellman.period and the fifth from bellman.trellis: period_joins(period), the joins of a period and its outputs; computable_together(period), its stage keys in layers; forward_order(period) and backward_order(period), its stage keys in the order of computation and in the reverse order; and inter_period_joins(mapping, later, earlier), the joins an inter-period connector makes. Each reads the fields of the period's elaborated stages; Period functions §4 states them.

The stage's own verbs, stage.calibrate, stage.methodize and stage.configure, are methods of the stage object, and the trellis verbs apply them to each stage occurrence, one elaboration of a stage file at one position of the trellis.

docs.title: 2 The record
docs.text: Every function that elaborates or binds reads records of one form: {"stage": {"text": text, "origin": origin}, "calibration": {...}, "settings": {...}, "methods": {...}, "provenance": {...}}. load_stage(path) of bellman.stage writes this form with the three mappings empty; load_trellis and load_recipe of bellman.trellis write it complete for every period. The three mappings are present even when they are empty, and None is not an empty mapping; a loaded methods mapping may hold a methods list, and the record's methods value is the mapping, never the list. label is the one optional key besides provenance, and a path string in place of the stage mapping is refused, since elaboration reads no file. Nothing that elaborates or binds merges anything: precedence is settled in the syntactic trellis, by load_recipe when a registry is read, or by the application when it writes the records itself.

docs.title: 3 The order of the bindings
docs.text: The bindings are made in the order calibrate, methodize, configure, on a trellis as on a stage. Configuration is defined on methodized versions only, because the settings are read against the methods that name them. A stage verb adds its binding to the stage it is called on and returns it; a trellis verb returns a new elaborated trellis and leaves its argument unchanged, and it binds a stage occurrence where the mapping the syntactic trellis holds at its key differs from what the stage occurrence holds, and copies it where it does not. The four stopping points, the symbolic trellis and the trellis after each verb, are therefore the results of the four calls, elaborate_trellis and then the three trellis verbs, each reading its mapping from the syntactic trellis given as its second argument. No call solves a model.

docs.title: 4 The refusals
docs.text:
A refusal of the factory is raised as FactoryError, which bellman.refusals exports, and carries a rule name under .rule. Each diagnostic names the rule, the address, the objects concerned and what to write. Each rule below links its entry on the Refusals page, which gives the rule's claim, its smallest example and the refusal that example provokes.

Rule Raised by When recipe-shape load_recipe the recipe has no stages key; a stage entry or a kind's block is not a mapping; a kind's block has no all list; periods: is not a pair; a range is not written lo-hi; two ranges overlap; a stage key is listed twice or has no file under stages/ recipe-source load_recipe a source name is written absolute or with ..; a source file is not in the registry; a parent: is not a name, or its chain cycles or exceeds ten files recipe-slot-unknown load_recipe a keyword names no slot of the recipe recipe-template-agreement load_recipe the recipe names a stage that no period of the trellis file holds, or a period holds a stage the recipe omits at a period it occupies slot-value-not-a-mapping load_recipe a slot is given a string fill-names-nothing load_recipe a fill key that no receiving stage declares and no registry block admits fill-mixes-kinds load_recipe a flat fill names both parameters and settings trellis-file-shape load_trellis, load_recipe, diagram_period, diagram_trellis a trellis file without periods, or a record without stage; a period index the trellis does not hold record-shape elaborate_stage; elaborate_trellis; calibrate_trellis, methodize_trellis and configure_trellis; the five functions of a period a path string, or a dictionary that is not a record, in place of the record; a record whose calibration, settings, methods or provenance is no mapping, or whose supplied digest or location disagrees with its text; two records of one digest whose texts differ; a position of the elaborated trellis that holds a record, a position of the syntactic trellis that holds neither a record nor a stage, or a record whose text differs from the version held at its position; a record at a key of a period whose joins are read, where an elaborated stage must stand period-join-cycle elaborate_trellis, accrete the authored pairs of a period form a cycle, or a connector joins a stage to itself connector-names-no-field elaborate_trellis, accrete a connector is no mapping or is written in the keyed form with other keys than from, to and fields, or two entries map one continuation field; a connector whose endpoint names no field, or several, is a diagnostic of the trellis's connection report and no refusal period-parameter-agreement elaborate_trellis, accrete; calibrate_trellis and configure_trellis for the values two or more stages of a period declare one parameter, or one setting in their additions, with sets that have no nonempty intersection the package reads, or supply it two values, or a value that lies outside a declared set readable-file load_stage; stage.calibrate, stage.methodize, stage.configure and load_trellis for a source file named by its path a path that names no .bl file, or a stage file that does not exist or cannot be read as UTF-8 text; a source file that does not exist, does not read as one YAML mapping, or writes a key twice

docs.title: Period functions
docs.text:
Summary

A period is a dictionary, {"stages": {key: record or stage}, "connectors": [...]}. accrete(trellis, period, inter_connector=None) of bellman.trellis appends one to a trellis, diagram_period(trellis, h) of bellman.period draws one, and period_joins(period) with three further functions of bellman.period and inter_period_joins of bellman.trellis read its joins and the order of its stages. No call constructs one period on its own: elaborate_trellis of bellman.trellis constructs the stages of every period of a trellis, and the order of a period's stages is derived from their fields, never from the template's list.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Periods: the period template and the joins between stages; Stage functions: the record and the stage. See also — The trellis factory: elaborating and binding every period of a trellis; Trellis Syntax §6: a trellis built by accretion on the durables model; The Bellman factory §7: the order of a period.

docs.title: 1 A period with one stage
docs.text:
A period holds one record for each stage occurrence, under its key, and the within-period connectors, which identify continuation fields of one stage with arrival fields of another. This period holds the discounting stage alone and needs no connector. From the repository root, the period's one record is written from the stage file, the period is appended to an empty trellis as its terminal period, and the trellis is elaborated and bound:

from bellman.stage import load_stage
from bellman.trellis import (accrete, calibrate_trellis, configure_trellis, elaborate_trellis,
                             methodize_trellis)

records = {
    "disc": {
        **load_stage("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/disc/disc.bl",
                     ["applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/disc/methods.bl"]),
        "calibration": {"β": 0.96},
    }
}
trellis = accrete({"periods": [], "inter_connectors": []},
                  {"stages": records, "connectors": []})
elaborated = elaborate_trellis(trellis)
specified = configure_trellis(
    methodize_trellis(
        calibrate_trellis(elaborated, trellis), trellis), trellis)
disc = specified["periods"][0]["stages"]["disc"]

The methods file of the discounting stage, read with the stage file by load_stage, types its two forward builders !deterministic and nothing else. The calls construct and bind one stage; they supply no terminal continuation value and solve nothing.

docs.title: 2 A period read from a file
docs.text:
A period template is the YAML file of one period, which lists its stage occurrences, as keys or as records, and its connectors. The template of the period of §1 reads:

!period
name: discounting_period
stages: [disc]
connectors: []

No call reads a template on its own: a trellis file names it, {template: period.yml, repeat: n} for a run of n equal periods, and the call that reads the trellis file reads the template with it. load_recipe(directory, recipe) of bellman.trellis reads a template that lists stage keys, as this one does, and the recipe supplies each key's record; Recipe functions §1 builds the smallest registry around this template. load_trellis(file), also of bellman.trellis, reads a template whose stages maps each key to a record, which names its stage file and gives its three mappings (The trellis factory §1). Either call returns a trellis whose periods have the form of §1. A key identifies a record and need not be the stage file's declared name; two uses of one stage file in a period take distinct keys.

docs.title: 3 accrete
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.accrete(trellis, period, inter_connector=None)

The call returns a new trellis with period appended at the end of periods, the period earlier in time, and inter_connector, the mapping from the continuation fields that leave it to the arrival fields of the period appended before it, written at inter_connectors[len(periods) - 2]; {} is written when none is given. The terminal period, appended first, takes no mapping, so len(inter_connectors) is len(periods) - 1, and no entry is reserved for the boundary: the terminal value is the continuation value a stage of the terminal period reads. No existing record is rewritten. The period may hold records, stage objects or both; the appended period is copied, its stages by a full copy, so that no object of the caller's stands inside the trellis, and a stage object placed by hand receives its position in its provenance on the copy. A stage object placed by hand is later copied by a verb as it stands, bound or not, since the syntactic trellis holds no mapping to bind it with.

Where every stage of the appended period is an ElaboratedStage, the package selects the period's connections and checks the inter-period mapping. Unresolved names, incompatible pairs, repeated endpoint claims and cycles remain inspectable through the connection report. Construction preserves those authored entries without certifying them for computation. Invalid source structure still raises an error. A period holding records is checked when the trellis is elaborated. The trellis passed in may itself be {"periods": [], "inter_connectors": []}: a trellis is built backwards from an empty dictionary, and elaborate_trellis and the three trellis verbs are loops of this call (The Bellman factory §3).

docs.title: 4 Stage order
docs.text:
Field dependencies determine the order of a period's stages, and the list order of the template carries no meaning. The joins are selected from authored connectors and the fields of the placed stages. An authored endpoint resolves to one continuation or arrival use, with a stage prefix where its bare name is ambiguous, and takes precedence over inference. Equal-name fields are inferred only where the package establishes a unique admissible connection; competing or cyclic inferred candidates remain unresolved. Several explicitly authored sources may reach one arrival field, with a separate complete-state route for each source branch. A continuation field that no selected join reads is an output of the period. The forward order, the backward order and the stages computable together follow from the joins; no graph is stored, and diagram_period of bellman.period draws the order on request (§5).

bellman.period.period_joins(period)                          # {"joins": [...], "outputs": [...]}
bellman.period.computable_together(period)                   # the stage keys in layers
bellman.period.forward_order(period)                         # the stage keys in the order of computation
bellman.period.backward_order(period)                        # the stage keys in the reverse order
bellman.trellis.inter_period_joins(mapping, later, earlier)  # the joins an inter-period connector makes

Each function reads a period whose stages are elaborated, specified["periods"][h] for instance; a period that holds a record is refused under record-shape, since a record has no fields. period_joins returns the joins, each written {"from": (key, field), "to": (key, field)}, and the outputs, the continuation fields that no join reads. computable_together returns the stage keys in layers according to the selected dependencies; this is an ordering query, not a certificate that every connection and numerical method is valid; forward_order returns the keys layer by layer and backward_order the reverse, the order in which the backward operators are applied. inter_period_joins(mapping, later, earlier) returns the joins an inter-period connector makes from later, the period appended later and so earlier in time, to earlier, the period it joins.

The order queries refuse a cycle among authored joins under period-join-cycle, with the involved pairs named. The construction and connection report retain that cycle for inspection. Remove or redirect an authored arrow to establish an acyclic order. Local fields may retain the same spelling in different stages. The connection report identifies unresolved endpoints and incompatible or incomplete routes; an unresolved arrow does not certify a complete composition.

Connections must join compatible fields with an unambiguous source and destination. Matching spellings alone do not establish compatible state domains or backward function components; Periods states these requirements. The order is separate from the semgraph, the semantic graph, inside each stage and from the syntactic trellis, which holds the mappings as data; ordering stage occurrences does not reinterpret their equations or prove that their numerical methods are compatible.

docs.title: 5 diagram_period
docs.text:
bellman.period.diagram_period(trellis, h)

The call returns a drawing of trellis["periods"][h], of the kind a graph's diagram() returns, which a notebook displays: one box per stage, labeled by its key, with the stage's declared name in parentheses beneath where the two differ, standing in the forward order from left to right; one arrow per join, labeled by the field it carries, field → arrival for an authored connection; and one unlabeled arrow to a plain label for each continuation field that no stage of the period takes. h counts periods before the terminal one, 0 the terminal period. The period's stages must be elaborated, since the joins are read from their fields; the drawing is built from the dictionary when it is asked for and stored nowhere.

docs.title: Recipe functions
docs.text:
Summary

load_recipe(directory, recipe, **fills) of bellman.trellis reads a registry through its recipe and returns the syntactic trellis, the model as written, with the three mappings of every stage occurrence merged from the sources the recipe names. assemble_trellis(directory, recipe, **fills), also of bellman.trellis, goes on to elaborate and bind that trellis and returns it specified. This page states what each reads, what it returns and what it refuses, and the form of the recipe.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — The Bellman factory §3: the registry and the recipe of the durables model; Model directory layout: the folders of a registry. Used by — The trellis factory: the functions that elaborate and bind the syntactic trellis a recipe gives. See also — Stage functions §3: the additions methodize reads.

docs.title: 1 The smallest registry
docs.text:
A registry with one stage, the discounting stage disc.bl of the portfolio application, needs eight files, which a model folder keeps in its subfolder declaration/ (Model directory layout). The stage file and its methods file stand in the stage's folder, stages/disc/disc.bl and stages/disc/methods.bl, the second an addition that opens with @methods: disc and types the two forward builders, arvl_to_dcsn.method : !deterministic and dcsn_to_cntn.method : !deterministic (Methodization); calibration/main.yml holds calibration: {β: 0.96} and calibration/near_terminal.yml holds calibration: {β: 0.98}; settings/main.yml holds settings: {}; the period template period.yml and the trellis file trellis.yml are:

!period
name: discounting_period
stages: [disc]
connectors: []

!trellis
name: discounting_example
periods:
  - {template: period.yml, repeat: 3}
inter_connectors:
  - {a: a}

The recipe, spec.yml, names the trellis file and the stage file by their paths from its own folder, and for the one stage and each kind an ordered list of sources, with a slot $fill in the calibration list and a range "0-1" that applies to the terminal period and the one before it:

trellis: trellis.yml
stages:
  disc:
    stage: stages/disc/disc.bl
    calibration:
      all: [calibration/main, $fill]
      "0-1": [calibration/near_terminal]
    settings:
      all: [settings/main]
    methods:
      all: [stages/disc/methods.bl]

One call reads the registry, here the folder declaration/ of a model folder discounting/, and binds the slot:

from bellman.trellis import load_recipe

syntactic = load_recipe("discounting/declaration", "spec.yml", fill={"β": 0.95})
syntactic["periods"][0]["stages"]["disc"]["calibration"]   # {'β': 0.98}: the range source stands after the fill
syntactic["periods"][2]["stages"]["disc"]["calibration"]   # {'β': 0.95}: the fill stands after the file

The index counts periods before the terminal one, so "0-1" is the terminal period and its predecessor, not the first two dates of life. The values satisfy the stage's declaration β : (0,1); loading does not check that they do, since it constructs no stage.

docs.title: 2 load_recipe
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.load_recipe(directory, recipe, **fills)

directory is the registry directory, recipe the name of its recipe file, and each keyword of fills binds the slot of that name. The call reads the recipe, the trellis file the recipe names under trellis:, the stage file each entry names under stage:, the period templates the trellis file names and every source file the recipe names, each once. It expands each {template, repeat} entry of the trellis file and repeats a single inter-period connector for each adjacent pair; puts each fill in its slot; merges each source list; and writes one record per stage and period, holding the stage's text and digest, its three merged mappings and the ordered sources that produced them. It returns the syntactic trellis: periods, inter_connectors, registry and provenance. Nothing is elaborated, and the stage files' declarations are read only to check the names a fill gives.

docs.title: 2.1 The recipe file
docs.text: The recipe is a mapping with three keys, and it names every file it reads by its path from its own folder, the registry directory. trellis: names the trellis file, trellis: trellis.yml, and is required. stages: maps each stage key to a mapping whose stage, required, names the stage file, stage: stages/disc/disc.bl; whose calibration, settings and methods blocks each hold an all list and any number of range lists keyed "lo-hi"; and whose optional periods: [lo, hi] restricts the stage to an interval of periods; a kind whose block is absent gets the empty mapping. registry: maps a kind to a list of sources whose names no stage declares. A calibration or settings source is named relative to the registry without its extension, calibration/main, and an addition with it, stages/disc/methods.bl; a slot is a $name. No file is read in place of a path the recipe does not write: an entry that names no stage file is refused even where a file stages/<key>/<key>.bl stands in the registry.

docs.title: 2.2 The merge
docs.text:
For a stage, a kind and a period, the list is the all list followed by the range list whose interval holds the period, if one does. The entries of a calibration or a settings list are merged in that order:

Values being merged Rule Mappings Merge matching keys recursively and add new keys. Scalars and ordinary lists The later value replaces the earlier one.

A later source changes the entries it names and keeps the rest. A methods list is not merged: the .bl additions it names are read in that order and unioned with the stage file when the occurrence is constructed, a component typed by two of them refused, so that the whole list is the stage occurrence's selection (The Bellman factory §3.2). The merge resolves data; it does not check that a method suits the equations it is attached to, which is the elaboration's work.

docs.title: 2.3 Slots and fills
docs.text:
A slot's position in its list is its precedence, a slot bound by no keyword contributes nothing, and the same slot may stand in the lists of several stages and kinds, where one fill is read wherever the slot stands. A slot name is a Python identifier other than directory and recipe. A fill takes one of two shapes:

Shape Example Read as Flat fill={"β": 0.95} read against the declarations of the stages that receive the slot; refused when it names both parameters and settings By kind fill={"calibration": {"β": 0.95}, "settings": {"n_a": 200}} split, each list taking the part of its kind

A mapping whose every top-level key is one of calibration and settings is read by kind; any other mapping is flat. For a calibration fill a stage declares its parameters; for a settings fill it declares the keys of the settings files its settings list names and the settings its methods files declare, read as they apply at each period the stage occupies, since a stage file declares no setting. A methods list takes no slot and a fill no methods part, which is refused under fill-names-nothing: a change of methods is a replacing selection, another addition named in the stage's list. The record's provenance holds, for each slot of each list, an entry {"slot": name, "bound": whether the keyword was given, "names": the fill's names the stage declares}.

docs.title: 2.4 The registry block
docs.text: A source named under registry: assigns names that no stage declares. They stand under the trellis's top-level registry key, {kind: {name: value}}, with their sources under the trellis's provenance, are bound to no stage, and are copied unread by elaborate_trellis and the trellis verbs; a fill of such a name changes the registry mapping and nothing else. They are data for the application's own functions, such as the function that evaluates the durables model's wage schedule.

docs.title: 2.5 Files and parents
docs.text: A source name resolves to the file spelled .yml or .yaml, and the file's kind is read from its top key, calibration or settings, not from its name or extension; an addition in a methods list is read whole, as the elaboration reads it, and a YAML file there is refused under recipe-source. A file may name a parent: source, which is read first and merged as an earlier entry of the same list; a parent chain is limited to ten files and may not cycle. The keys parent, description, version and __comment__ of a source file are not part of the mapping it contributes.

docs.title: 2.6 Refusals
docs.text: Each refusal is a FactoryError carrying its rule name. recipe-shape: the recipe has no stages key, or names no trellis file; a stage entry or a kind's block is not a mapping; a stage entry names no stage file; a kind's block has no all list; periods: is not a pair; a range is not written lo-hi; two ranges of one stage and kind overlap; a stage key is listed twice. readable-file: the path an entry writes under stage: names no file, or no .bl file, refused as load_stage refuses it, at the address stages.<key>.stage. recipe-source: a source name is written absolute or with ..; a source file is not in the registry; a parent: is not a name, or its chain cycles or exceeds ten files. recipe-slot-unknown: a keyword names no slot. recipe-template-agreement: the recipe names a stage that no period of the trellis file holds, or a period holds a stage the recipe omits at a period it occupies, the stage and both files named. slot-value-not-a-mapping: a slot is given a string. fill-names-nothing: a fill key that no receiving stage declares and no registry block admits, the receiving stages and their declarations named; a fill with a methods part. fill-mixes-kinds: a flat fill names both parameters and settings. trellis-file-shape: the trellis file has no periods, or a record has no stage.

docs.title: 3 The syntactic trellis it returns
docs.text:
The result is a dictionary and is read by key. Every adjustment to the model, a fill, a value that differs by period or a replacing selection, is made in it before elaboration and binding.

Access Result syntactic["periods"][h]["stages"] the records of period h, by stage key, h = 0 the terminal period syntactic["periods"][h]["stages"][key]["calibration"], and ["settings"], ["methods"] the merged mappings of that stage at that period key in syntactic["periods"][h]["stages"] whether the stage is active at h syntactic["periods"][h]["stages"][key]["provenance"]["source_lists"] the ordered sources of each mapping, with paths, digests and slot entries syntactic["inter_connectors"][h] the mapping joining periods[h + 1] to periods[h] syntactic["registry"] the registry-level names by kind syntactic["provenance"] the recipe and the trellis file with their paths and digests, and the sources of the registry block

The syntactic trellis holds no stage, no graph and no solution.

docs.title: 4 assemble_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.assemble_trellis(directory, recipe, **fills)

The call returns the specified trellis that load_recipe(directory, recipe, **fills), elaborate_trellis, calibrate_trellis, methodize_trellis and configure_trellis make in this order, each verb given the syntactic trellis of the first call, and copies each stage occurrence once. It refuses whatever any of the five refuses, in the same order. A family of fills is a sweep, [assemble_trellis(directory, recipe, fill=f) for f in fills]; an estimation is the same expression inside its criterion function.

docs.title: Stage functions
docs.text:
Summary

load_stage(path) of bellman.stage reads one stage file into a record, and elaborate_stage(record), also of bellman.stage, constructs from it a symbolic stage, whose semgraph, the semantic graph, holds the typed fields and equations of the file. The stage's three verbs, calibrate, methodize and configure, each return a new version with one binding written, in that order.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Stages and Methodization: declarations and supported computations. Used by — Period functions and The factory API: constructing independent stage occurrences. Formal account — Appendix C: the assumptions needed to interpret equations as functions.

docs.title: 1 Loading and specifying a stage
docs.text:
The discounting stage leaves assets unchanged and multiplies the continuation value and the marginal value by its discount factor. From the repository root:

from bellman.stage import elaborate_stage, load_stage

stage = elaborate_stage(load_stage("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/disc/disc.bl"))
calibrated = stage.calibrate({"β": 0.96})
methodized = calibrated.methodize("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/disc/methods.bl")
specified = methodized.configure({})

The addition methods.bl beside the stage file types the two forward builders of the discounting stage as deterministic and binds nothing else. The example binds the discount factor and supplies neither a solver nor a terminal continuation value; the empty settings mapping suffices because the addition declares no setting. The trellis verbs apply the stage's three verbs to each stage occurrence of a trellis.

For consumption, save the complete constrained stage of Field equations as cons.bl, and write its methods file as Methodization §8 describes: a block policy that types the endogenous grid method and brings its lines, and the derivative lines of the value builders. The methods file states how the stage is computed; it adds no boundary condition the stage file leaves out and proves no optimality.

docs.title: 2.1 load_stage and elaborate_stage
docs.text:
record = bellman.stage.load_stage(path)
stage = bellman.stage.elaborate_stage(record)

path is a string or Path naming a .bl file. load_stage reads the file and returns its record: the text and the origin under stage, the calibration and the settings empty, under methods the additions whose paths are given beside the stage file's, load_stage(path, [addition]), none by default, and the origin and the digest of the text under provenance. Nothing is parsed, and a caller completes the three mappings before elaboration binds them. elaborate_stage parses the record's text, constructs the stage at the record's origin with the record's provenance, binds the sources the record supplies, and returns the ElaboratedStage: the symbolic stage where the record supplies no source or bind=False is given, as for the record load_stage returns (The stage §1); it reads no file. Given a path string, or a mapping that is not a record, it refuses under record-shape and says to write elaborate_stage(load_stage(path)). The temporary syntax tree and source-span table are discarded after construction; the retained semgraph holds the interpreted equations and typed definitions.

The application's helper load_stage(name, lib) has a different signature and resolves a module reference within a library; it is not load_stage(path) of bellman.stage. A caller that already holds a parsed term uses make_stage(term, spans) of bellman.stage, with the second argument supplied explicitly; a decoded term can use spans=None.

docs.title: 3 Methodization
docs.text:
stage.methodize(addition)

addition is the path of a .bl methods file, the addition beside the stage file, or a list of such paths applied in the order given (Methodization). The call reads the additions with the stage file's tree, elaborates the stage anew from their union and returns the stage, whose read-only methods binding is keyed by the place at which each method is kept: the entry policy.method : !egm is kept on the policy builder, policy; a representation, cntn_to_dcsn.evaluate.method : !Linear, at the Evaluation it names; and a handler, policy.handler : "cons-port:egm", beside the method of its place (Methods and places). A call is the whole selection of the stage: the additions it names replace those read before, so a change of methods is made by calling methodize again with the other file. A component typed by two of the additions is refused under declared-twice, the refusal naming both files. A record assembled by hand takes its additions from load_stage(path, additions) (§2.1).

An authored block describes a typed computation, and a method binds only at a place the stage holds: a builder, a line with an id, a line marked !node, an operator written in a line, a declared function, or the Evaluation that closes the policy builder or a backward value builder, at which a representation is written (Methods and places §1). A statement marked !node is a place of its own, and its computation a sub-builder. An inspection address or a nested mathematical operation alone creates no place. Appendix D §§3 and 6 tells an authored node from an operator occurrence inside an equation and states how an address names each.

An operator written in a line receives a method by its path from the block, E_Ψ_θ.method : !gauss_hermite(n_Ψ=n_Ψ_nodes, n_θ=n_θ_nodes) in the header of the block cntn_to_dcsn, without an added !node; a !node place requires its own authored identifier. These paths select computations without turning every containing statement into an authored node.

A component typed twice, a method word the catalogue lacks and a path that names no place are refused, the refusal naming the entry and, for a path, the stage's places. No method word supplies a missing equation.

docs.title: 4 Calibration and configuration
docs.text:
stage.calibrate(calibration_source)
stage.configure(settings_source)

Each source is a path or a mapping, and each call adds its binding to the stage it is called on and returns that stage. Calibration requires a value for every declared parameter, in the parameter's declared set, and stores them in the calibration binding, leaving the parameter names symbolic in the equations; extra names in a shared source are not bound, and a value for a derived parameter, which calibration evaluates from its definition, is refused. Retained conditions on the parameters alone are decided at the values: a false condition refuses, a true one is established with the values as evidence, and an undecided one remains required. Configuration requires prior methodization and a value for every setting an attached method references, names in nested grids or mappings included, and stores the values in the settings binding; the method records keep the authored setting names.

The bindings are made in the order calibrate, methodize, configure. Applying calibrate or configure again returns another version with the new values, the earlier version unchanged, and every version has its own copies of the graphs, sharing nothing with the version it came from. Mathematical domains remain declarations of the model; numerical grids and tolerances belong to the selected methods and settings.

docs.title: 5 Inspecting a stage
docs.text: An ElaboratedStage has seven attributes, name, metadata, definitions, initial, _builders, bindings and provenance, the fifth the stored record of the builders graphs that stage.builder reads, and answers questions through them and through its own methods; The stage and the pages after it state each with its printed form. par lists the declared parameters with their sets and, once calibrated, their values, and par["ρ"] answers one of them, whose .value is the bound value; settings lists each setting value with the place that reads it and the method that reads it, and settings["n_a"] answers one of them; methods prints the method bound at each place, and methods["policy"] answers the one bound at the place the methods file writes; places() lists the addresses that can receive a method; obligations() lists the conditions the construction states, each with its status; each of the stage's four graphs answers diagram() with a drawing, stage.builder.bwd.diagram() for the backward builders; and print(stage) prints the stage's sheet, its printed view (The stage §3). bindings holds the three bindings, which par, methods and settings read, and provenance holds the origin, the text and the digest of the file, the source of each binding, the version of the package and the digests of its grammar files, and on a bound version the verb that made it, its source and, under parent, the provenance of the version it was made from, together with the stage occurrence's position and the ordered sources of its record when it stands in a trellis. Every projection is read-only; a version is never adjusted in place.

docs.title: The trellis factory
docs.text:
Summary

A trellis is a dictionary, {"periods": [...], "inter_connectors": [...]}, its terminal period first. The functions of bellman.trellis act on it: load_trellis(file) reads one from a trellis file; elaborate_trellis constructs its stages; calibrate_trellis, methodize_trellis and configure_trellis bind them; specify_trellis constructs and binds them in one call; respecify_trellis binds again the stage occurrences whose records changed; changed_positions lists what a verb bound, a copy of a binding among them (The Bellman factory §6); and diagram_trellis draws the periods with their inter-period connectors.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Trellises: period indices and records; Period functions: accretion and the order of a period. See also — Recipe functions: the syntactic trellis a registry gives; The Bellman factory §5: what each call prints on the durables model.

docs.title: 1 The trellis file
docs.text:
A trellis file, trellis.yml by convention, lists the periods of a model. Its periods list writes a period out, its stages and its connectors, or gives {template: <period file>, repeat: n} for a run of n equal periods, and its inter_connectors list holds one mapping per adjacent pair or one mapping that stands for every pair. Two readers of bellman.trellis read the form. load_trellis reads a file whose stages are records: each names its stage file under stage, gives its calibration and its settings inline or as paths to files, and names its methods as the path of a .bl addition beside the stage file or a list of such paths, read in the order written, every path relative to the file's directory; a stage with no methods reads no addition. load_recipe reads a file whose stages are named by key, the recipe supplying each stage's source and mappings (Recipe functions §2). A file of the first kind, with a terminal period written out and two equal periods before it:

periods:
  - stages:
      cons:
        stage: stages/cons/cons.bl
        calibration: calibration/ρ.yml
        settings: {n_m: 10, n_a: 10, a_min: 0.001, a_max: 10.0}
        methods: stages/cons/methods.bl
    connectors: []
  - {template: period.yml, repeat: 2}
inter_connectors:
  - {a: m}

Here period.yml writes the same record for cons without the methods, and the one mapping {a: m} stands for both adjacent pairs.

docs.title: 2 load_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.load_trellis(file)

The call reads the trellis file at file, each period template it names and each stage file once, for its text and digest, and returns the syntactic trellis: periods, one record per stage and period with its three mappings and, under provenance, the origin and digest of the stage's text and the ordered sources of each mapping; inter_connectors, one mapping per adjacent pair; and, under the trellis's own provenance, the file's path and digest. A mapping given as a path is read from that file. A single standing mapping is read at repeat: 1 as well, where it stands for no pair and inter_connectors is empty. A file without periods, or a record without stage, is refused under trellis-file-shape. Nothing is elaborated. The package writes no file of constructed stages: a trellis is rebuilt from its source records, whose provenance holds the path and digest of every source.

For a source editor, bellman.trellis.read_trellis_file(file, texts=None) expands the period templates and inter-period mappings without loading stage files or constructing stages. The returned period records retain the stage keys or records as written. texts may supply proposed file contents by resolved path; the result records the digests of those contents. This lets an editor check changed connectors against its existing stage occurrences.

docs.title: 3 elaborate_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.elaborate_trellis(syntactic, previous=None)

The call returns the elaborated trellis, symbolic: the same dictionary with an ElaboratedStage at every key. It constructs each distinct stage text once per origin and places a full copy at each of its positions, each copy carrying its position in its provenance; copies a position that already holds a stage, the copy at its new position; and, given previous, copies from it every position whose record has the digest and origin of the stage held there and constructs the others, which is how a changed stage file alone is constructed again while the rest is kept. Every other key of the argument, inter_connectors, registry, provenance and an optional solutions list, is copied. The connections are selected from the fields and authored connectors, including mappings between periods. Missing or ambiguous endpoints, incompatible connections, repeated endpoint claims and cycles remain recorded as connection problems on the returned model. Read them with connection_report (§9). A returned object does not imply that every connection is valid or that the model can yet be computed. The call binds nothing; the calibration, settings and methods stand in the records and are read by the verbs.

The call keeps every check the elaborator makes: the shape of the trellis and of each record, and a supplied digest or location that disagrees with the source; a refusal names the affected stage occurrence. It writes into the provenance of each stage occurrence the label of its record, where the record has one, and, under versions, the version of the package and the digests of its grammar files, read once per call. It takes its own copies of each record's mappings, so a later change to the caller's dictionary alters no stage occurrence, and a source-shape, stage-construction or inconsistent period-parameter failure raises without returning a partial trellis. Connection diagnostics, by contrast, are available on the returned object (§9). It is built period by period by accrete, and it merges nothing: precedence is settled in the syntactic trellis before the call.

docs.title: 4 calibrate_trellis, methodize_trellis and configure_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.calibrate_trellis(elaborated, syntactic)
bellman.trellis.methodize_trellis(elaborated, syntactic)
bellman.trellis.configure_trellis(elaborated, syntactic)

Each verb takes the elaborated trellis and the syntactic trellis it is to be bound with, and returns a new elaborated trellis. For each period h and key, it reads the mapping of its own kind, syntactic["periods"][h]["stages"][key]["calibration"] for calibrate_trellis, and applies the stage's own verb, stage.calibrate or stage.configure, to the stage occurrence at the same key of the elaborated trellis where that mapping differs from what the stage occurrence holds: for calibration, in a value at a name the stage declares, compared by numeric equality; for settings, in any value. methodize_trellis binds nothing: the additions a record names under methods are read with the stage text when the occurrence is constructed (The Bellman factory §6), so it copies each stage occurrence whose record names the additions it was constructed with, by their paths and the digests of their texts, and refuses one whose record names others under record-shape, the change being a construction, made by elaborate_trellis(syntactic, elaborated) or specify_trellis(syntactic, elaborated) (§3, §4.1). The trellis verb applies the stage's verb once for each distinct stage occurrence and mapping and places a copy of the result, equal to what the stage's verb gives there, at the other positions of that pair (The Bellman factory §6). A stage occurrence whose mapping is unchanged is copied, as is one at a key where the syntactic trellis itself holds a stage object, a period built by hand. The verbs are applied in the order calibrate, methodize, configure; configure_trellis is defined on methodized stage occurrences, since the settings are read against the methods that name them.

A parameter name that two or more stages of one period declare names one parameter of the period, shared by those stages, and the same spelling in another period is another parameter (Periods §5). The elaboration reconciles the declarations of such a parameter in each period: sets that are one set agree, and sets the package reads, a real set or an interval with numeric endpoints, agree in their intersection, so that ℝ₊ in one stage and ℝ₊₊ in another make the parameter's set ℝ₊₊; two sets whose intersection is empty, or is not one the package reads, are refused under period-parameter-agreement, with the period, the parameter, the stages and their declarations named, and no value establishes such an intersection. calibrate_trellis then supplies the parameter once for the period: the value the sources of the declaring stages give it, after the precedence among each stage's own sources, which the stages whose own sources do not supply it take as well; two sources that give it two values, and a value that lies outside the set a declaring stage writes, are refused under the same rule, with the period, the parameter, the stages and their sources named, and the refusal names the stage occurrence and the kind in its notes as a stage verb's refusal does. A stage occurrence placed by hand keeps its own calibration, which counts among the values the period's sources give.

Three properties hold of the verbs, on a trellis as on a stage. The sources are merged before a verb binds, so no verb resolves precedence, and a verb refuses a source that values fewer names than the stage requires. The last binding stands: calibrating a version twice gives the bindings of calibrating it once with the second source, its methods and settings kept, and the same for configuring; a stage occurrence whose additions changed is constructed anew with them by elaborate_trellis(syntactic, elaborated), then calibrated and configured with the values and the settings its record holds. Binding changes no graph: the semgraphs, the semantic graphs, of a bound version equal those of the symbolic one. Appendix G §7 states the three trellis verbs, with their mappings held fixed, as maps from stage versions to stage versions. A verb's refusals are the stage verb's: a calibration that values fewer names than the stage declares, a method word that is unknown or a path that names no place, a settings source that lacks a name an attached method reads.

docs.title: 4.1 specify_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.specify_trellis(syntactic, previous=None, kinds=KINDS)

The call returns the trellis that elaborate_trellis(syntactic, previous) (§3) and then the verbs of kinds return. kinds names any of the three kinds of mapping a record holds, "calibration", "methods" and "settings", all three by default, as KINDS holds them; the verbs are applied in the order calibrate, methodize, configure, whatever order kinds writes, and a kind that is none of the three is refused with a ValueError. Each distinct stage text is constructed once, or taken from previous as elaborate_trellis takes it, and each stage occurrence is copied once, where the elaboration and each verb copy every occurrence. The call refuses what that route refuses, and a refusal of a binding names the stage occurrence and the kind in its notes, Stage occurrence: <address> and Binding kind: <kind>. assemble_trellis(directory, recipe, **fills) is specify_trellis(load_recipe(directory, recipe, **fills)) (Recipe functions §4).

docs.title: 4.2 respecify_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.respecify_trellis(specified, before, syntactic, kinds=KINDS)

The call returns the trellis that specify_trellis(syntactic, kinds=kinds) returns, where specified is the trellis that specify_trellis(before, kinds=kinds) returned for an earlier syntactic trellis before. A position whose record is the same in both syntactic trellises keeps the stage occurrence specified holds there; every other position is constructed, bound and copied as specify_trellis does it. A record holds its stage's text, its three mappings and the digest of each file read for them, so that a change of one stage's text, calibration, methods or settings binds that stage's occurrences again and no other, except that a changed value of a parameter the stage shares with other stages of its period (§4) binds those stages' occurrences in that period again as well, since the period supplies them the changed value. The two syntactic trellises must hold the same periods, the same stage keys and the same connectors; otherwise the call refuses under trellis-file-shape, and such a trellis is specified whole by specify_trellis. A trellis given with occurrences bound under other kinds than kinds is refused under record-shape.

docs.title: 5 changed_positions
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.changed_positions(before, after)

The call returns the list of positions (h, key) whose stage occurrence in after is a new version of the one in before, or stands at a position before lacks. A verb writes the earlier version into the new one's provenance as its parent, a copy of a binding included, and a copy of an unchanged stage occurrence keeps its provenance equal, so the two provenances are compared; the length of the list is the count of what a verb bound, a copy of a binding among them, since it is a new version of its position (The Bellman factory §6), and the count of stage occurrences less that length is what it copied unchanged.

docs.title: 6 diagram_trellis
docs.text:
bellman.trellis.diagram_trellis(trellis, periods=None)

The call returns a drawing of the periods of an elaborated trellis, every one or those whose indices periods lists, of the kind a graph's diagram() returns. Each period is drawn as diagram_period draws it, inside a frame labeled periods[h] with h and, where the trellis's registry holds last_age, the age last_age − h; the drawing's labels name each stage periods[h] <key>, its period's address and its key. The terminal period stands at the right and the earlier periods to its left, so that economic time runs from left to right and the backward computation from right to left, the two directions written in the drawing's title. Every inter-period connector inter_connectors[h] whose two periods are drawn is drawn as wires from the continuation fields that leave periods[h + 1] to the arrival fields of periods[h], each wire labeled with the mapping's index and its field pair; a period with no mapping to its neighbor is drawn with no wire. The drawing is built from the dictionary when it is asked for and stored nowhere; the trellis is not itself a graph object. The same trellis is read interactively in Google's Model Explorer, where each period and each stage occurrence inside it is a box that opens with a click, and each join is drawn between the wires of the two occurrences it joins (The view in Model Explorer §5).

docs.title: 7 Period indices and the terminal value
docs.text: The index h counts periods before the terminal one. periods[0] is the terminal period, periods[h + 1] lies one period before periods[h], and inter_connectors[h] joins the continuation fields that leave periods[h + 1] to the arrival fields of periods[h], so that backward computation proceeds from h = 0 to larger h. The terminal value is the continuation value that a stage of the terminal period reads, for the durables model the bequest stage, whose continuation value is zero and is supplied as boundary data at realization; no entry of inter_connectors is reserved for it, and len(inter_connectors) is len(periods) - 1.

docs.title: 8 The entries of a model's files
docs.text:
from bellman.trellis import (
    append_to_mapping,
    append_to_sequence,
    connector_entry,
    entry_span,
    entry_value,
    insert_in_sequence,
    period_entries,
    remove_from_mapping,
    remove_from_sequence,
    replace_entry,
    split_entry,
    written_at,
    written_spans,
)

These functions read and edit one entry of a recipe, a trellis file, a period file or a calibration, settings or methods file as text, or find the entry that writes a part of a trellis, so that a program edits a model without rewriting its files. An entry is named by its address, written as the factory's refusals write one, stages.cons.methods.all[0] or periods[0].connectors[0]. entry_span(text, address) answers the line and the column of the entry's value and those just after it, counted from one, the columns in code points; entry_value(text, address) answers the value as the package's reader of YAML files reads it, every tag kept, and refuses with a ValueError a text that does not read as YAML or that holds a value the reader cannot build, such as !!bool abc; and replace_entry(text, address, written) answers the text with that value's characters alone replaced by written, a string, a number, a boolean or a tag, so that the comments, the other entries and the layout stay as written. A string is written within the value's quotes where the value is written in single or double quotes, and otherwise plain, or in double quotes where the plain text would read as another type than a string; a number or a boolean is written plain as YAML writes it, 1.05, 400 or true, and a tag, given as entry_value reads it, {"__yaml_tag__": "pchip", "value": ""}, plain as !pchip. The result is read back, and one in which the entry does not read as written, or another entry changed, is refused, as is a mapping or a list given as written. append_to_mapping(text, address, key, value) and append_to_sequence(text, address, item) answer the text with one entry, key: value or item, added at the end of the mapping or the list at address, on a line of its own after its last entry where the collection is written in block style and before its closing brace or bracket where it is written in flow style, every other character kept; the result is read back, and one in which the collection does not hold its former entries and then the new one is refused. insert_in_sequence(text, address, index, item) answers the text with item placed before the item at index of the list at address, on a line of its own just before that item's line where the list is written in block style and before the item, followed by a comma, where it is written in flow style, an index equal to the list's length appending item; the result is read back as an append's is. split_entry(text, address, at) answers the text with the entry at address, an item of a list that writes repeat: n, written twice in its place, the first time with repeat: at and the second with repeat: n - at, so that {template: period.yml, repeat: 6} split at 3 becomes two entries that each write repeat: 3; an entry that takes its repeat from the period file it names is refused, since the entry does not write the repeat. remove_from_sequence(text, address, index) and remove_from_mapping(text, address, key) answer the text with the item at index of the list at address, or the key key of the mapping there with its value, taken out, the lines of the entry going with the comment lines just above it where it is not the first, and a collection whose only entry goes written [] or {} in its place, so that {a: k} becomes {} and the list of inter-period mappings keeps its length; the result is read back, and one in which the collection does not hold its former entries but the one taken out is refused. written_at(file, address) moves an address of the trellis that load_recipe or load_trellis expands, periods[5].connectors[0], to the file and the address that write it, here period.yml and connectors[0] where the trellis file's entry {template: period.yml, repeat: 14} writes the period. period_entries(file) answers, for each period of that expanded trellis, the file and the address of the entry that writes the period and every period that entry writes, reading the trellis file once. connector_entry(trellis, writing, reading, texts=None, *, selection=None, replacing=()) answers where the connector from the continuation field writing to the arrival field reading of an elaborated trellis is written, each field given as (h, key, field): a ConnectorEntry that names the file, the address, the periods the line reaches and the line itself, {m_next: m} in a period's connectors or m_next: m in an inter-period mapping, or, for two fields that no connector may join, the reason, with no exception raised: not-adjacent where the reading field stands neither in the writing field's period nor in the next period in time, port-joined where a join already reads the continuation field, since a continuation field joins one arrival field, no-mapping where the file writes no list or mapping to hold the line, and name-shared where no compact spelling, including qualified endpoints, resolves to the chosen pair at every period reached by the shared source. The writer tries bare names first, then qualifies only the endpoints that need their stage key. A key containing dots is separated from its field at the final dot. selection may reuse the selected result for this exact trellis version. To move an inferred arrow, replacing names its selected pair; its writing port becomes available to the replacement. An authored arrow must first be removed from its mapping. The writer checks source resolution; the caller checks compatibility of the complete proposed connection set before saving it. An arrival field that a join already reaches takes a further source, as an arrival field may take several (Trellis §2): the line is then a further key of the connector of the period that writes such a join, {a_nxt_adj: a_bq} added to {a_nxt_kp: a_bq, …}, where the connector is flat or names the two stages of the drag, and otherwise a line as for an arrival no join reaches, so that the number of mappings never changes. Bellman Workbench edits a recipe's entry through replace_entry when a file is chosen for a cell of its recipe table, and the entry of a calibration, settings or methods file when a parameter's value, a setting or a method's tag is written in its BellmanType panel (Bellman Workbench §2), adding through append_to_mapping the value of a parameter that no file writes and the method of an entry that names none; it adds a stage or a period to a model folder it wrote through append_to_mapping and append_to_sequence.

An existing connector key is preserved even when its destination is unresolved. The writer tries an available qualified spelling; if the proposed entry would replace an existing key, it returns source-authored and identifies that mapping. Correct or remove the existing entry before asking to replace it.

docs.title: 9 Inspect the selected connections
docs.text:
from bellman.trellis import connection_report, to_model_explorer

report = connection_report(trellis)
view = to_model_explorer(trellis, periods=(0, 1), selection=report.selection)

connection_report(trellis, *, periods=None, stages=None, selection=None) returns pairs of resolved field uses, complete-state routes, diagnostics, rejected automatic candidates, unjoined fields, effective bindings, operation counts, the selected result and the source file. A route is one source stage's ordered continuation state on a branch mapped to one destination stage's ordered arrival state. A certified route has established the state map, joint law and required backward value components; a visible pair alone does not establish those claims.

Each pair identifies both period indices, stage keys, local fields and perches, whether it was authored or inferred, and its compatibility judgment. An authored pair also records source_address, source_key and source_value: the expanded mapping address and exact written endpoints. written_at(file, pair.source_address) finds the physical mapping, including a shared period template. Inferred pairs have no authored source entry. The original address continues to name the connector group.

A period or stage restriction filters the report's pairs, routes, diagnostics, rejected candidates, unjoined fields and bindings. Its selection and counts still describe the complete trellis. Reuse selection only with the exact stage occurrences, connectors and effective bindings that produced it; a changed reading requires a new selection. The report, Model Explorer view and unpaired_joins can share that result, so changing a display restriction does not require another selection or stage construction.

docs.title: 9.1 Inspect an unfinished model
docs.text:
Ordinary construction returns an inspectable model when the stage declarations can be constructed but their connections are incomplete or invalid. There is no separate draft flag. Inspect the reasons before using a complete connection:

report = connection_report(trellis)
print(report)
report.diagnostics
report.rejected
report.unjoined

diagnostics contains the rule, affected address and a specific reason. An incompatible pair is different from one whose compatibility cannot be established with the available declarations or values. rejected explains why automatic candidates were not selected, including comparisons that require an unavailable parameter value. A count of zero selected pairs must not hide these reasons.

unjoined separates internal and exterior field uses; each contains writing (continuation) and reading (arrival) entries. The exterior entries are the earliest period's arrival uses and the terminal period's continuation uses. An open field can be intentional while constructing a model. A field with a selected pair can still have a type error, so read the diagnostics and route status as well as this list. An operation that needs a certified route refuses an uncertified one; ordering stages refuses a cyclic dependency.

A diagnostic's source_entries retains each authored origin as (address, source_key, source_value). Use written_at(report.file, address) to find the physical source file and its local mapping address, then entry_span on the current file text for its position. A shared period source can concern several occurrences, and a route can cite several entries. For several origins, written_spans(report.file, addresses, texts=None) returns one (path, EntrySpan) or None per requested address, in the same order. Include the source key in the address to locate that exact mapping entry. The query reads period expansion once and composes each physical source once for its spans; texts supplies current unsaved text by resolved path. A missing or unreadable origin returns None without hiding other available origins. An inferred candidate has no authored connector entry; its field occurrences identify the declarations to inspect. Models built in memory without source provenance still provide occurrence addresses, but no physical file is invented.

docs.title: The stage
docs.text:
Summary

elaborate_stage turns one stage file, a .bl file, into one Python object, the stage. This page states how a stage is made, the seven attributes it holds and the questions it answers about itself: its printed view, its contents, its fields, its conditions, its diagnostics and its encoding. Every listing is printed by the package from the consumption stage applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Stage tutorial: the stage file line by line. Used by — The initial diagrams, The builders graphs and the pages after them: the pieces reached from the stage. See also — API: the functions that make a stage in §2.1 and every path of the stage in §2.4; The factory API: the functions that load, elaborate and bind a trellis of stages.

Each python block on this page runs after the blocks above it, in one session started at the repository's root, and the text below a block is what that block prints.

docs.title: 1 Making a stage
docs.text:
A stage file holds declarations and blocks. Each block lists the fields it reads and the fields it writes, and it denotes an operator: on value functions when it is read backward, on finite measures over the states when it is read forward. The consumption stage of the portfolio application, from which the listings of these pages are printed, is the running example. The household holds resources m at the arrival perch; the block arvl_to_dcsn writes m_d = m at the decision perch, where consumption c is chosen, and the block dcsn_to_cntn writes savings a = m_d - c. The policy block states the choice by its maximization, the line optimality; the three lines of the endogenous grid method, InvEuler, grid and identification, stand in the methods file beside the stage file, methods.bl, which A builder §2 reads one by one after methodization (Methodization). The block cntn_to_dcsn writes the value V and states its derivative in m_d by a derivative line, D_{m_d}V = 𝑑𝑢(c). The line InvEuler of the methods file reads the derivative of the continuation value in a by the derivative term D_{a}V[>]; neither derivative is a field of a header. The file, as the repository holds it:

from pathlib import Path

print(Path("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl").read_text(), end="")

@stage: cons

Xm := ℝ₊₊
Xa := ℝ₊

ρ : [1, inf)

𝑢(c : ℝ₊₊) := c^(1-ρ)/(1-ρ)         :: [id=util]
𝑑𝑢(c : ℝ₊₊) := c^(-ρ)               :: [id=marginal_utility]
Γ(x : ℝ₊₊) := (0, x]

[id=arvl_to_dcsn, (m : Xm, l : ℝ₊) : !arvl -> (m_d : Xm) : !dcsn] {
    m_d = m
}

[id=dcsn_to_cntn, (m_d, c : !ctrl @ ℝ₊₊) : !dcsn -> (a : Xa) : !cntn] {
    a = m_d - c
}

[id=cntn_to_dcsn, (V[>] : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu, c) : !cntn -> (V : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu) : !dcsn] {
    V        = 𝑢(c) + V[>]          :: [id=value]
    D_{m_d}V = 𝑑𝑢(c)                :: [id=marginal]
}

[id=dcsn_to_arvl, (V) : !dcsn -> (V[<] : ℝ @ !vlu) : !arvl] {
    V[<] = V                        :: [id=value]
}

[id=policy, (V[>] : [-inf, inf) @ !vlu) : !cntn -> (c : ℝ₊₊ @ !ctrl) : !dcsn] {
    c      = argmax_{cp : Γ(m_d)}(𝑢(cp) + V[>])   :: [id=optimality]
}

load_stage(path) reads a stage file into its record, a dictionary that holds the file's text and origin under stage, the calibration and the settings as empty mappings, under methods the list of the additions it read, [] for the stage file alone, and the file's origin and digest under provenance; load_stage(path, [methods_path]) reads the stage file with the methods files its list names, and methods then holds one record with the keys origin and text for each addition, in the order given. elaborate_stage(record) parses the text and constructs the stage. The result is a stage occurrence: the file elaborated once, with its own bindings, sharing no object with any other elaboration of the same file. One file may be elaborated at several positions, in one period or across periods, and each elaboration is a separate stage occurrence, which prints the name the file declares and, when it stands in a trellis, records its position there in its provenance. A stage occurrence is never adjusted in place: it varies only through one of its three bindings or through a different text, which is elaborated again, and a text derived from the file is elaborated as a stage occurrence of its own, with its origin recorded.

from bellman.stage import elaborate_stage, load_stage

stage = elaborate_stage(load_stage("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl"))
print(repr(stage))

ElaboratedStage('cons', symbolic)

The short form names the class, the declared name of the stage and its version. Where the bindings present follow the order calibration, methodization, configuration from its start, the version is one word: symbolic before any binding, then calibrated, methodized and specified as the verbs of The binding verbs are applied in that order. Otherwise the version is the list of the bindings present, in that order: a stage occurrence constructed with its methods files and not yet calibrated prints methods, and methods, settings once it is configured.

A record may also hold, as mappings, the sources of the calibration and the settings, and under methods the additions load_stage read, which are read with the stage text when the stage is constructed and bound by no verb: elaborate_stage(record) constructs the stage from the stage file with its additions and binds each source the record supplies, in the order of The binding verbs §1, a non-empty calibration as calibrate binds it and a non-empty settings as configure binds it. Under methods anything but that list is refused under record-shape, the mapping {"methods": []} among it, and the refusal says to write methods: []; an empty mapping is admitted as the empty source of a record written by hand. An empty source binds nothing, so the record load_stage(path) returns gives the symbolic stage, as above, and elaborate_stage(record, bind=False) gives the symbolic stage whatever the record holds, the additions left out with the other sources. The stage is constructed, the bindings are made on it, and it is copied once, at the end; for a record without additions the result equals, provenance included, the stage the two verbs bind one after another on elaborate_stage(record, bind=False) with the record's own mappings, each binding that stage itself. A source is refused as its verb refuses it.

record = load_stage("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl")
record["calibration"] = {"ρ": 6.0}
calibrated = elaborate_stage(record)
print(repr(calibrated), calibrated.par.ρ)
print(repr(elaborate_stage(record, bind=False)))

ElaboratedStage('cons', calibrated) 6.0
ElaboratedStage('cons', symbolic)

Two further functions of bellman.stage construct the same kind of object. elaborate_text(text, origin) elaborates a text held in memory and records origin as its source. make_stage(term, spans) constructs a stage from a syntax tree that parse_with_spans, of bellman.syntax.lower, has already read, where spans holds the source positions that a refusal cites, or is None for a tree without positions; calling the two separately distinguishes a parsing error from a construction error.

from pathlib import Path

from bellman.stage import elaborate_text, make_stage
from bellman.syntax.lower import parse_with_spans

text = Path("applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print(repr(elaborate_text(text, "applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl")))
term, spans = parse_with_spans(text, filename="cons.bl")
print(repr(make_stage(term, spans)))

ElaboratedStage('cons', symbolic)
ElaboratedStage('cons', symbolic)

A stage keeps no syntax tree: the tree is discarded once the stage is constructed, and every later answer is read from the stage. A file that construction cannot read is refused with a ConstructionError, which names the file position, the rule the file does not satisfy and what to write instead; a form of the language that no construction rule reads is refused with NotConstructed, a kind of ConstructionError. Both are exported by bellman.refusals, and Refusals gives an example of every rule.

docs.title: 2 The seven attributes
docs.text:
A stage is a frozen record, a Python object whose attributes cannot be reassigned once it is built, with seven attributes and no others. definitions, initial and _builders state the model, the third under a private name: it is the stored record of the two builders graphs, which a reader reaches through stage.builder (The builders graphs §1); bindings holds the three bindings of this version; provenance records the file, its digest and where each binding was read from.

import dataclasses

print([field.name for field in dataclasses.fields(stage)])
print(stage.bindings)
print(stage.provenance)

['name', 'metadata', 'definitions', 'initial', '_builders', 'bindings', 'provenance']

settings      none   configure(stage, source)
origin   applications/portfolio-choice/declaration/stages/cons/cons.bl
sha256   e60110b0b964ce482812c558922bc7aa6eaaf14421e2e162b9f87cc7b120a667
Attribute Python type What it holds name str the name the stage declares metadata read-only mapping the file's @ lines other than @stage definitions read-only mapping from an identity to a Definition every declared name once, and one record for each line of a block initial record of two graphs the graphs on fields, backward and forward _builders record of two graphs the graphs on functions and measures, backward and forward, which stage.builder reads by the pair of perches each builder joins bindings record of three mappings the calibration and the settings of this version, each None until bound, and blocks, the rows a solution method's lines add at the operative level, by the builder each opens; the methods of a version are no binding but the components of its signatures, read from the typing entries of the definitions table (Methods and places) provenance read-only mapping the file's path, text and digest, under versions the version of the package and the digests of its grammar files, and under sources where each binding was read from and its digest; on a bound version, the verb that made it, its source and, under parent, the provenance of the version it was made from; for a stage occurrence in a trellis, also its position there

Nothing else is stored. Whatever the definitions, the graphs and the bindings determine is computed when it is asked for, and the answer is then kept on the version it was asked of. calibrate and configure keep the answers the stage had computed from the definitions and the graphs alone, which neither changes, and discard those that read a binding, which the stage computes again when they are asked for; methodize elaborates the stage anew from the union of the stage file with its methods file, whose entries and lines enter the definitions table and whose solution method's lines change the operative builders, and keeps only the answers of the stage file's own construction and of the initial diagrams (The binding verbs §1). Of the three bindings, the calibration completes the economic problem, and the methods and the settings record how it is to be computed, changing no assertion of the model.

print(stage.name, len(stage.definitions))
print(sorted(stage.provenance))

cons 17
['origin', 'sha256', 'sources', 'text', 'versions']

The attributes that hold the model, the mapping of the builders and the three tables read from the model answer objects of their own, each of which has a page; the three perches answer objects too, which have a section, The builders graphs §2:

for name in ("definitions", "initial", "builder", "arvl", "dcsn", "cntn", "par", "settings", "methods"):
    print(f"stage.{name:<12} {type(getattr(stage, name)).__name__}")

stage.definitions  Definitions
stage.initial      Initial
stage.builder      BuilderPairs
stage.arvl         PerchHandle
stage.dcsn         PerchHandle
stage.cntn         PerchHandle
stage.par          Parameters
stage.settings     Settings
stage.methods      BoundMethods

stage.definitions is the definitions table; stage.initial holds the initial diagrams; stage.builder reaches each builder by the pair of perches it joins; of the three perches, stage.arvl and stage.dcsn each reach the builders of the edge that leaves the perch, the step from that perch to the next, and stage.cntn, which no edge of the stage leaves, refuses both directions with the reason (The builders graphs §§1 and 2); stage.par and stage.settings are the parameters and the settings; and stage.methods holds the bound methods. No attribute can be assigned after construction, and no answer changes the stage: a version with other bindings is a new object.

docs.title: 3 The printed view
docs.text:
stage.view() answers the stage's printed view, a text the package writes each time it is asked and stores nowhere; print(stage) prints the same text. It lists the perches with their fields, the fields by role, the blocks with the fields they read and write, the definitions by kind, the four graphs, the bindings and the directions of the two initial diagrams. Its block signatures come from the file, the inputs, the outputs and the perches of each block as its header declares them; the rest are the package's own summaries, such as the count of definitions by kind.

print(stage.view())
