docs.text: matsya-master has one role of its own, the conversation role; when a question names a stage file that the elaborator accepts, it also calls Semantics-to-Prose, to describe that file. The conversation role receives the question, pages of the reference guides, the passages of the index that match the question, the session's text, the outputs of the job it discusses, the selected job or the latest job that Matsya in three parts §3 names, and, when the question names a stage file, the dossier of that file once the elaborator accepts it, with Semantics-to-Prose's account of it, or the elaborator's refusal; it may ask the program for more pages, more passages, the outputs of the session's other jobs or a job's stage files a bounded number of times. It returns an answer with citations, each a quoted sentence of what it read, and the program accepts no citation it cannot find in that material. It writes no stage file. When the user asks it to build or to submit, it sets one field of its reply and the program starts a job from the session; it starts no job otherwise.

docs.title: 3 Which command for which request
docs.text:
The request What runs The command a question about a model, about the language, about why a judge disagreed, about what a job produced one turn of the conversation role, a few calls of a language model, taking less time and costing less than a job bellman-matsya ask <session> "…" build a declaration from a description one job of all the roles of §1, several minutes, charged by the language-model tokens of every call bellman-matsya job submit model.md --target stage (a session is created for the file; the target, which Matsya in three parts §2 defines, names what the job returns, a stage, a period, a trellis or a recipe) rebuild it after an edit of the description a new job, as above, in the same session: the edited text is appended to the session, and the job reads the session's whole text, the earlier description included bellman-matsya job submit model.md --session <session> --target stage; a second bellman-matsya job submit model.md --target stage would create a second session build from the discussion so far the same job, started by the conversation role from the session's text bellman-matsya ask <session> "Submit this as a job." answer a question of matsya-architect the reply appended to the session; the first reply to the job's questions starts the next job with the reply in its text, unless a later job of the session has started bellman-matsya session add <session> reply.md --replies-to <entry> read what a job produced, or its report of what did not match nothing on the server; the client writes the folder and the report bellman-matsya job files <job> <folder> see the jobs of a model, their labels and the selected job, when one is selected; with none selected, the listing does not name the job the conversation discusses, which Matsya in three parts §3 defines nothing on the server; a listing bellman-matsya session show <session> make the conversation discuss another job of the session, one that holds a record a mark on the session bellman-matsya session select <session> <job> stop a job that is queued or running a queued job is cancelled at once; a running job ends before its next call, and a call already sent is charged bellman-matsya job cancel <job> search the documentation, and the literature your Matsya token may read, without a question the index alone, no role bellman-matsya search "…", and bellman-matsya search "…" --collections literature for the literature

Two rules follow for an assistant acting for a user. A job costs money and minutes and is started only when the user asks to build; a question costs little and is the way to understand a result before building again. And a job's questions are answered in the session, all of them in one reply file, not by editing the files: the next job reads the session's text, and the first reply starts it at once. A later reply to the same questions starts nothing, and one that arrives while that job runs is not in its text, so the job ends marked built from an earlier version and appends no question to the session.

docs.title: Working with Matsya from the command line
docs.text:
Summary

This page follows one piece of work through the command bellman-matsya, from installation to the folder of stage files, with the commands as you type them and what each prints. The command is matsya-client of Matsya in three parts: a program that sends your requests to the service and writes what comes back. Service commands take --json to print the service's answer unchanged; project commands use it to print an answer assembled from the project folder and the service. The bare bellman-matsya command, configure and docs have no JSON form. bellman-matsya <command> --help lists a command's options.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Matsya in three parts, which defines the three parts and the words session, job, turn, version, label and target, and The roles and the work of a job, which names the roles whose steps bellman-matsya job wait prints. Continued by — Working on a project folder, the same work done in a model's own folder, which remembers the model's session. See also — The command reference, every option, printed line, exit status and JSON field of the commands this page uses; Stages and Constraints in the language guide, for reading the stage files a job writes. Explained for developers in — the Matsya developer guide.

docs.title: 1 Installing and setting up
docs.text:
The package bellman-matsya-client installs the command bellman-matsya and the Python module bellman_matsya; it needs Python 3.10 or newer. Install it from the public Matsya repository, whose root is the package. This needs Git, but no Bellman checkout on your computer:

python -m pip install git+https://github.com/econ-ark/matsya.git
bellman-matsya --help

To update the client, run python -m pip install --force-reinstall git+https://github.com/econ-ark/matsya.git. The client installation does not install or start the service.

The public Matsya repository holds this client alone: the earlier package econ-ark-matsya, which installed the different command matsya, was removed from it on 16 October 2026, and the current Bellman installation does not remove a copy already installed on your computer. If you no longer use it, remove it from its Python environment with python -m pip uninstall econ-ark-matsya, or use pipx uninstall econ-ark-matsya for a pipx installation. To find command installations, use type -a matsya bellman-matsya on macOS or Linux, or Get-Command matsya,bellman-matsya -All in PowerShell. Use bellman-matsya for Bellman work.

The service's administrator gives you a new token beginning msy_. The client uses the Bellman service at http://45.55.225.169:8710 automatically. This preliminary HTTP connection sends the token and your requests without encryption. Keep the token private. Run:

bellman-matsya configure
bellman-matsya index

configure, run without an option, asks only for the token, then saves it in ~/.config/bellman-matsya/config.toml without contacting the service. It retains a custom service address already saved in that file; otherwise the client uses its built-in address. This file survives a package upgrade. BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN and BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER override saved values, so remove outdated values before configuring a new token. The earlier ~/.config/matsya/config.toml and MATSYA_TOKEN or MATSYA_SERVER variables are not read. At the first use with neither a Bellman configuration file nor BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN, the command prints two lines directing an assistant to bellman-matsya docs --all; an upgrade with an existing configuration file does not print them. index checks access and prints the digest of the material Matsya can retrieve, the embedding model and the configuration version. A refused request or connection error needs correction before a job is submitted. The command does not print the token in its later output.

An earlier .matsya/project.json is not read by this client. Keep your authored economics.md and declaration/, then run bellman-matsya project init in the model folder to create a Bellman session and its .bellman-matsya/ metadata. Working on a project folder gives the remaining steps.

docs.title: 1.1 Your own Anthropic API key
docs.text:
Once the Matsya token is saved and bellman-matsya index has succeeded, you may add a personal Anthropic key, an Anthropic API key of your own, so that the language-model calls of the jobs and questions you start are charged to your own Anthropic account in place of the service's account (Matsya in three parts §1). The key is optional and never replaces the Matsya token, which is still sent with every request. The whole procedure, in its fixed order, is:

  1. The service's administrator registers you and gives you a Matsya token.
  2. bellman-matsya configure saves the token, and bellman-matsya index checks it against the service.
  3. bellman-matsya configure --set-anthropic-key asks for your Anthropic API key at a prompt and saves it on your machine; or you set BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY for one shell session instead.
  4. bellman-matsya alone shows which key the next job or question will use; job submit, project submit, ask and session add --replies-to then send the key with the request, and the line Credential: your Anthropic API key in the answer confirms that the service ran the work with it.
  5. bellman-matsya configure --clear-anthropic-key removes the saved key when you no longer want it used.

The paragraphs below give each step's details. Step 3 is

bellman-matsya configure --set-anthropic-key

The command asks for the key without showing the characters you type, removes any spaces or line breaks around it, and saves it in ~/.config/bellman-matsya/anthropic-key, a file beside config.toml that only you can read; run again, it replaces the saved key. It prints the file's path, states that the jobs and questions you start are then charged to the Anthropic account of that key, and names the command that removes it. A key that is empty or contains a space, a line break or another character that an HTTP header does not allow is refused, and nothing is saved. On a machine where no Matsya token is configured, neither saved by configure nor set in BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN, the command asks for nothing, writes nothing and exits with status 1 after the sentence Error: no Matsya token is configured. A personal Anthropic key is an addition to a Matsya token, not a substitute for it: save the Matsya token the service's administrator gave you with bellman-matsya configure, or set BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN. bellman-matsya configure --clear-anthropic-key deletes the file and says whether a saved key was removed, after which later jobs and questions use the service's key, unless BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY is set and not empty; configure without an option leaves a saved key in place. Type the key yourself at the prompt, in your own terminal: it is never an argument of a command, and an assistant never asks for it, receives it in chat or types it.

The environment variable BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY, when it is set and not empty, supplies a key without saving it, and the client then uses it in place of a saved key. Set it from a private file, so that the key is never typed on the command line, where the shell keeps its history:

export BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY="$(cat <the private file that holds your Anthropic API key>)"

Every command that contacts the service checks the selected key first and, for a key with the fault described above, prints one sentence that names the variable or the saved file and the remedy, and exits with status 1 (The command reference §2.2). The client sends the key in the header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key, beside the Matsya token, with three kinds of request alone: the submission of a job, by job submit or project submit; a question, by ask; and a reply of the kind user, the default, that names a question with session add --replies-to, which may start a job's next attempt (§3). Every other request, such as those of index, search, job status, job wait, job export and session show, is sent with the Matsya token alone, and the key never appears in a request's body, in a session's entries or in anything the client prints. Because the service keeps no key, a reply that would start the next attempt of a job run with a personal key must include a key again; without one, the service refuses the reply and leaves the session as it was.

The client sends the key only to an HTTPS address, or to a service on your own machine at an http address whose host is written localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1. The address http://45.55.225.169:8710 uses plain HTTP and therefore cannot receive a key: while a key is selected, job submit, project submit, ask and session add --replies-to are refused there before their first request, so that no session, entry, job or turn is created, with the sentence Error: A personal Anthropic key is sent only over HTTPS or to localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1, and the service address is http://45.55.225.169:8710; use an HTTPS address, or stop selecting the key: unset BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY, run bellman-matsya configure --clear-anthropic-key, or omit anthropic_api_key. and status 1. The client never sends such a request without the key, so your work never runs under the service's key in place of yours, while commands that send no key, such as index, search and job status, work at that address as before. The service, for its part, accepts a personal key only when its operator has enabled personal keys, which the service at that address has not done. Until the service's administrator announces an HTTPS address, a personal key can therefore be used only with a service on your own machine or through an encrypted tunnel, such as an SSH tunnel, to a loopback address.

A personal key changes the account that is charged, not the bounds on what a job or a question may use. Every configuration recorded since 9 October 2026, the service's default among them, bounds all the language-model calls of one job by 3,000,000 input tokens and 300,000 output tokens, and those of one turn by 600,000 input tokens and 60,000 output tokens; a call that would pass a bound is not made, and the job or the turn ends with the reason token_ceiling_reached (What Matsya reads §4). Anthropic charges each call at its prices for the language model that the role names, and the record of each job and turn reports under usage the tokens charged.

The client and the service report in three places which key the service uses for a piece of work. bellman-matsya alone prints, after its line on the Matsya token, one line that says which key the next job, question or reply will use, and never the key (The command reference §2.1). The service records for each job and turn the field credential_source, client when its calls were made with your key and service when they were made with the service's key, and never the key or any part of it. A command that sent your key prints Credential: your Anthropic API key when the service reports client for the new job, turn or attempt, and job status and job wait print the same line for such a job; when the service reports service, or reports nothing, as a service built before personal keys does, the command prints its usual lines, then Error: the service at <address> accepted <job or turn> <id> under its own Anthropic key, not yours., for a job also Cancel it with: bellman-matsya job cancel <id>, and exits with status 1. If Anthropic refuses the key, a job fails with the code provider_rejected_credential, and a turn ends incomplete with that reason, after one request and with no request under another key. When the work's credential_source is client, save a valid key with bellman-matsya configure --set-anthropic-key or remove it with --clear-anthropic-key; when it is service, the service's own key was refused, and the service's administrator should be told.

docs.title: 2 A job from a description
docs.text:
Write the model's description in a Markdown file, with the states, the choices, the constraints, the shocks, the timing and the objective in prose and displayed equations. Then:

bellman-matsya job submit model.md --target stage

The option --target names the job's target, what the job is to return, stage, period, trellis or recipe, as Matsya in three parts §2 defines them; the command refuses a submission that names none, before any request. The command creates a session named model, after the file, appends the file's text to it as entry 1, and starts a job from that session. It prints the session's identifier and name, the entry's number, the job's identifier and its state queued, and two lines: how to follow the job, and how to see the session, where the job's questions and your replies are kept. --name "Household with firms" gives the session another name; --max-cycles 2 permits two iterations after the initial declaration, hence at most three declarations and their elaborated semantic objects; --no-session submits the file as the job's source with no session, in which case the job's questions stand in its record only.

bellman-matsya job wait <job>

The command polls the job and prints a line whenever its step or iteration changes, naming the step and the role that computes it, among the roles of The roles and the work of a job §1: preparation (the Model-prose-writer and the prose-source-judge), writing (Prose-to-Bellman-Sym and elaboration, first for the initial declaration and then once per iteration), prose_writing (Semantics-to-Prose) and judging (the prose-roundtrip-judge). The program compares adjacent elaborated semantic objects after writing. When the job ends it prints the final state and its reason: converged; not_converged, with the reason, such as the cycle limit reached; needs_input, with the numbered questions and a sentence that says whether they stand in the session; or failed, with its code. bellman-matsya job status <job> prints the same without waiting.

bellman-matsya job files <job> proposed-model

The command writes the job's products into the folder, which must be new or empty: the available stage files under declaration/stages/<key>/<key>.bl, the writer's note, when it leaves something open, beside a single stage as <key>.md and otherwise as declaration/notes.md, any period, trellis, calibration, settings or methods file under declaration/ by its name, the prose paired with those files as economics.md, the report as report.md, and the record the service returned as record.json. Run it for a not_converged job too: it saves any work the job produced, while the report says why the checks did not conclude. If no declaration file was produced, the folder contains only the prose, report and record that exist. The report states the job's label, its final state and reason, the iterations run, what each judge found, whether the adjacent elaborated semantic objects are equivalent, the questions and the language-model tokens charged. --all-iterates adds iterates/initial/ and one iterates/cycle-<n>/ folder per iteration, with each declaration and its input prose, plus the complete record.

docs.title: 3 Replying to a job's questions
docs.text:
A job that ends needs_input has written its questions into the session as entries, provided you added no entry to the session while it ran; otherwise they stand in its record alone, where bellman-matsya job status prints them, and you submit again. Read them and reply:

bellman-matsya session show <session>
bellman-matsya session add <session> reply.md --replies-to <entry number>

The reply is an entry of the session, and because it answers a question of the session's latest job, it starts the next job at once, with the text as it now stands. Follow it with bellman-matsya job wait. A reply is kept in the session but starts nothing when a later job of the session has started since the question was asked, or when an earlier reply to the same job's questions has already started its next attempt; submit again instead, with bellman-matsya job submit --session <session>.

docs.title: 4 Asking questions in a session
docs.text:
bellman-matsya ask <session> "Which equation characterizes the optimal consumption choice in this model?"

matsya-master answers from the retrieval index, the session's text and the outputs of the session's jobs. The command waits for the turn and prints, when the answer read a job's outputs, the line Answer from with the label and identifier of the job it used; then the answer; then the citations, each with the passage's path or the output's address, the heading, the page where the index records one, and the quoted sentence. Questions that end in a request for more information from you are printed as such. --stage-file <path> attaches a stage file of your own to the question; the service elaborates it and the answer reads its dossier (The roles and the work of a job §1).

A session may hold nothing but questions and answers, created with bellman-matsya session new "a name" and fed with bellman-matsya session add <session> notes.md; and a question may be asked in the session bellman-matsya job submit created, in which case, once the job has ended with a record, the answer reads that job's outputs.

docs.title: 5 Asking matsya-master to submit a job
docs.text:
In a session, after some discussion, you may ask in words:

bellman-matsya ask <session> "Submit this as a job."

matsya-master recognizes the request, starts a job from the session's text as it then stands, your request included, and answers with the job's label and identifier; the command prints the line to follow the job. With --follow proposed-model the command stays attached to that job, prints its steps, and writes the folder of §2 when it ends. Without the option the job runs on the server all the same, and bellman-matsya job wait follows it later. A question that merely mentions a job starts nothing: the role submits only on a request to build or to submit.

docs.title: 6 Several jobs on one model
docs.text:
Each submission from a session is a new job with the next number, and the session lists them with their labels:

bellman-matsya session show <session>

matsya-master discusses the session's selected job or, when none is selected, the latest job that Matsya in three parts §3 names; the questions you ask after that job ended do not change which job it is. To discuss another job of the session that holds a record, select it; to stop a queued or running job, cancel it:

bellman-matsya session select <session> <job>
bellman-matsya job cancel <job>

A job cancelled while it runs keeps its record and the usage of the calls it had made; a provider request already sent completes before it stops, and the interface promises nothing else. A job cancelled while queued never runs and holds no record. Cancelling a job that has already ended is refused with the sentence that the job has ended.

docs.title: 7 A paper
docs.text:
A paper is submitted as its text, in a Markdown or LaTeX file, and marked as a paper with --paper:

bellman-matsya job submit paper.md --paper --target stage

The command creates a session named paper, after the file, appends the paper's text to it as an entry of the kind paper, and starts the job from that session; --name gives the session another name, and --session <session> appends the paper to a session you already have and starts the job from it. The job reads the session's text as a paper: the Model-prose-writer quotes the passages of the paper on which the model prose rests, each with the heading it stands under where a heading stands above it, and the job goes on only when every quotation is found in the session's text and, where a heading is given with it, under that heading. Because the paper is an entry of the session, a job that ends needs_input appends its questions to the session after the paper; you reply to them there as §3 describes, and ask about the paper and the job's outputs in the same session (§4). --no-session sends the paper as the job's source with no session, and its questions then stand in its record only. Without --paper a file is a description. bellman-matsya session add <session> paper.md --kind paper appends a paper to a session without starting a job.

A PDF is refused before any request, with the sentence A paper is sent as Markdown or LaTeX text; convert the PDF first.; convert it to Markdown or LaTeX and submit that file. The paper's text is sent to the language-model provider; ask the service's administrator before submitting a paper that may not leave your machine.

docs.title: 8 The commands
docs.text:
The table lists the commands of this page. The command reference gives each command with its options and their defaults, the lines it prints, its exit statuses and the fields of its --json answer, and Working on a project folder follows the commands of a project folder.

Command What it does bellman-matsya, bellman-matsya docs [<page>] [--online], bellman-matsya docs --all [--online], bellman-matsya docs --path what Matsya is, where its guide is installed and whether a Matsya token is saved; this guide's pages in Markdown, as installed with the client or, with --online, as its public repository holds them today bellman-matsya configure saves your Matsya token and retains any custom service address already saved bellman-matsya configure --set-anthropic-key, bellman-matsya configure --clear-anthropic-key after the Matsya token is configured, saves or removes your optional personal Anthropic key bellman-matsya index the index the service reads, the embedding model and the configuration's version bellman-matsya search "<query>" [--collections …] [--limit n] the passages of the index that match a query bellman-matsya job submit <file> --target <stage\|period\|trellis\|recipe> [--paper] [--name …] [--max-cycles n] [--no-session], bellman-matsya job submit --session <session> --target … starts a job, from a file through a session it creates, or from a session's text bellman-matsya job status <job>, bellman-matsya job wait <job> a job's state, once or until it ends bellman-matsya job files <job> <folder> [--all-iterates] [--overwrite] writes the products, the report and the record into a folder bellman-matsya job cancel <job> cancels a queued or running job bellman-matsya session new "<name>", bellman-matsya session add <session> <file> [--kind …] [--replies-to n], bellman-matsya session show <session>, bellman-matsya session select <session> <job> or --none the session's record bellman-matsya ask <session> "<question>" [--stage-file <path>] [--follow <folder>] one question answered by matsya-master

docs.title: Working on a project folder
docs.text:
Summary

This page follows one project folder, a model's own folder that keeps the model's session, from bellman-matsya project init to bellman-matsya project pull, with what each command prints, and shows a job's files written back into the folder or into a sub-folder of it.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Working with Matsya from the command line, the commands of a session and a job, and For an assistant using Matsya §4, which defines the project folder and gives its commands in order. Continued by — Reaching the service by HTTP, the requests that the commands send, for a user without the client.

docs.title: 1 Begin with the model's files
docs.text:
Suppose the folder household/ contains the description you wrote in economics.md and a stage file at declaration/stages/household/household.bl. Other project folders may also contain period, trellis, recipe, methods, calibration or settings files. For an assistant using Matsya §4 defines this layout and the target, the level of declaration the job is asked to return. This example has no such additional files, so its target is stage.

From inside household/, run:

bellman-matsya project init

The command creates a session named household, appends the text of economics.md as its first entry, and prints its session identifier. Its output includes these lines, with the identifier and folder path filled in:

Project folder: <absolute path to household>
Session <session>: household
Entry 1: the text of economics.md
Wrote .bellman-matsya/project.json and .bellman-matsya/README.md
Wrote AGENTS.md, whose paragraph points an assistant to .bellman-matsya/README.md
Submit the model, in the project folder, with: bellman-matsya project submit

The file .bellman-matsya/project.json records the session identifier, the service address and a digest of economics.md used to recognize later edits; it holds no Matsya token. The short .bellman-matsya/README.md names the files and commands of this folder. If AGENTS.md already exists, init leaves it unchanged and prints the paragraph for you to add. If economics.md is absent or empty, the session has no entry yet; write the description before submitting the model.

docs.title: 2 Submit and inspect a job
docs.text:
In the same folder, run:

bellman-matsya project submit
bellman-matsya job wait <job>

Use the identifier in the Follow it with: bellman-matsya job wait <job> line printed by submit. The submission sends the session's text and the declaration files already in the folder. It lists each file sent as the starting declaration, the files the job first checks, and names any files it leaves out. A stage page such as declaration/stages/household/household.md is left out: it explains the stage but is not a declaration file. For this example, the printed lines include Starting declaration: household.bl and Target: stage, read from declaration/. The command then prints the job's label, its identifier, its initial state and the command for following it. Use --target period, --target trellis or --target recipe only when you want a different level from the one the folder implies; --max-cycles <n> limits its cycles of writing and checking.

The description is not appended again when its bytes have not changed since the session last received it. After you edit economics.md, the next bellman-matsya project submit appends the new text as another session entry before starting its job. bellman-matsya project status tells you whether it has changed. It prints the session identifier and version of its text, its numbered entries, its jobs with their labels, any selected job, any question awaiting a reply, and the commands for asking or answering a question. Use bellman-matsya job wait <job> to observe when a queued or running job ends. A job can end converged, not_converged, needs_input, cancelled, failed or interrupted; an ended job is not necessarily a declaration to keep.

docs.title: 3 Ask or answer a question
docs.text:
If the job ends needs_input, run bellman-matsya project status and read its question. If an entry was added to the session while the job ran, its questions remain in the job record instead; read them with bellman-matsya job status <job>. For a question that awaits a reply in the session, project status gives its entry number and a line of this form:

Reply with: bellman-matsya session add <session> <file> --replies-to <entry number>

Put your answer in a text file and run that line with the actual file path. A reply to a question from the job currently waiting for input starts one new job; the command prints its identifier and Follow it with: bellman-matsya job wait <job>. If a later job has already started, the reply remains in the session but starts no job. To ask about the model or a job's result, use the other line printed by project status:

bellman-matsya ask <session> "<question>"

This asks matsya-master, the part of Matsya that answers questions in a session. It does not write a stage file. The project has no separate project ask command; the ordinary bellman-matsya ask and bellman-matsya session add commands use the session identifier that project status prints.

docs.title: 4 Write a job's files
docs.text:
Inspect the job's final state and report before deciding where its files belong. bellman-matsya project pull chooses the latest ended job of this session that holds a record; bellman-matsya project pull <job> names a particular job. By default it writes a complete model folder into bellman-matsya-output/job-<number>/. You can name a different new or empty sub-folder with --into <subfolder>:

bellman-matsya project pull
bellman-matsya project pull <job> --into second-look

The command first prints the status and source sections of the job's report, then Wrote <n> files to <subfolder>: and the paths it wrote. The job's model prose is economics.md inside this output sub-folder; the project's own economics.md and declaration/ are unchanged. Use a new sub-folder for the second command; a nonempty one is refused.

When you want the job's declaration in the project folder, run:

bellman-matsya project pull <job> --replace

This writes each returned declaration file to its corresponding path under declaration/, marking a file it replaced with (replaced) in the printed list. It writes report.md and, when the job holds model prose, model-prose.md. An open writer's note goes to .bellman-matsya/writer-note.md, apart from an author's stage page. It never writes the user's economics.md, and it keeps existing declaration files the job did not produce, listing them after the files written. --replace and --into cannot be used together. The command reference gives every option and the exact fields of the --json answer.

docs.title: 5 Work with an assistant and the Workbench
docs.text: An assistant can read .bellman-matsya/README.md and bellman-matsya docs --all, run these commands for you, and use --json on the project, job, session and ask commands to read their structured answers. You can open the same model folder in the Bellman Workbench to inspect its stage files. The service keeps the session's entries and job records; bellman-matsya project status reads them from it each time. A pull into a sub-folder also writes a copy of the job's record there as record.json. You decide which job to inspect and whether to replace local files.

docs.title: Reaching the service by HTTP
docs.text:
Summary

The commands of matsya-client send their requests to the Matsya service over HTTP, the protocol of the web, and print its answers, and a reader without Python, or a program written in any language, can send the same requests directly. This page lists every route of the service, that is, every kind of request, named by an HTTP method and a path, with the body the request sends and the answer it receives. It says how the Matsya token is sent with each request, how a personal Anthropic key may be sent with a request that starts language-model work, and how the service refuses a request, and it gives a curl example for each kind of request: the index, a search, a job from a description, a job's record, a session, an entry, a question and its answer, a cancellation and the selected job. For each route it names the command of matsya-client that sends the same request.

Relationship with other documents

Builds on — Matsya in three parts, which defines the session, the job, the turn, the label and the target; The roles and the work of a job, which names the roles whose work a job's record reports; Working with Matsya from the command line, whose commands send the requests of this page. Continued by — The command reference, the first of the reference pages, which gives the exact form of every command of the client. See also — Collections and weights, the fields of a search and what a returned passage holds; The Python module and the files the client writes, the same requests as Python functions. Explained for developers in — the Matsya developer guide, which describes the program that answers each route.

docs.title: 1 The address, the Matsya token and the examples
docs.text:
The service's administrator gives you two things: the service's address, a URL, and your Matsya token (Matsya in three parts §1), msy_ followed by 32 hexadecimal characters, which the service checks on every request under /v1/. Every session, job and turn you create belongs to you, and the service answers a request for another person's as though it did not exist (§3).

The examples on this page read the two from environment variables, the same two that the command bellman-matsya reads, so that a terminal set up for the examples serves the command as well:

export BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER="<the service's address, without a final slash>"
export BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN="$(cat <the private file that holds your Matsya token>)"

Keep the Matsya token in a file that only you can read and that stands outside every folder under version control; reading the variable from that file keeps the Matsya token out of the shell's history.

Every request to a route under /v1/ carries the Matsya token in the Authorization header, after the word Bearer and one space:

Authorization: Bearer msy_…

A request with a body sends one object in JSON, the text format of named fields and lists that the service reads and writes, with the header Content-Type: application/json, and every answer is one JSON object. The examples use curl, the command-line program for HTTP requests that most systems install, in version 7.76 or later. Its option -sS hides the progress display and keeps curl's own error messages, and --fail-with-body prints the service's answer to a refused request and makes curl exit with a nonzero status. An answer arrives on one line; a JSON viewer, or python3 -m json.tool where Python is installed, prints it with one field per line.

The first request checks the address and the Matsya token:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/index" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

The answer names the version of the retrieval index by its digest (Matsya in three parts §1); the identity of the embedding model, the model that turns each passage into a vector of numbers for the search (Collections and weights §4); the ID and the version of the default configuration, the instruction texts and settings under which the service runs (§8); the service's own version; and its capabilities, the features of the service that a client uses only where this answer names them:

{"index_digest":"…","embedding_model_id":"…","configuration_id":"…","configuration_version":"…",
 "service_version":"…","capabilities":["capture_at_acceptance","job_delivery_id"]}

The service names two capabilities: capture_at_acceptance, that it fixes a job's source material when it accepts a job whose request names reviewed_through (§6), and job_delivery_id, that a job's request may name a delivery_id (§5). A service whose answer names no capabilities refuses both fields of a job's request with 422. bellman-matsya index sends the same request and prints its first four fields, and bellman-matsya configuration effective sends it to report the configuration under which a new job or question would run, with the service's version and its capabilities (The command reference §9).

A request that starts language-model work, that is, a job, a question or a reply that starts a job's next attempt, may also include a personal Anthropic key, an Anthropic API key of your own (Matsya in three parts §1), in the header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key; the service then makes every language-model call of that job or turn with your key, and Anthropic charges those calls to your Anthropic account in place of the service's:

Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key: <your Anthropic API key>

The key is an addition to the Matsya token, not a substitute for it: the service checks the Matsya token first, and a request with a key and no valid Matsya token is refused with 401. The service reads the header on three routes alone, POST /v1/model-iterations, POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns and POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/entries, and accepts the key only when its operator has enabled personal keys. A service that has not enabled them refuses a request whose header holds a key with 403 and creates nothing (§3), and a service built before personal keys ignores the header and runs the work under its own key. The service holds the key in memory for that job or turn alone, never stores it, and records only which key it used, in the field credential_source (§5). Send the header only to an HTTPS address, or to a service on your own machine at localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1: over plain HTTP between machines the key is sent unencrypted, and the address the client uses by default, http://45.55.225.169:8710, uses plain HTTP, so never send the header there. To send a key with curl, read it from a private file into the variable that bellman-matsya also reads, as the Matsya token is read above, and add -H "Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key: $BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY" to a request of those three routes:

export BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY="$(cat <the private file that holds your Anthropic API key>)"

docs.title: 2 The routes
docs.text:
A part of a path in braces stands for an identifier that an earlier answer gave: the id of a session, a job or a turn, 32 hexadecimal characters, or the passage_id of a passage, 64 hexadecimal characters. A query parameter is a named value written into the address after the path, following ?, in the form name=value, as in /v1/model-iterations/<job>?view=full.

Method and path Body Answer The same request from bellman_matsya-client GET /v1/index none the index's digest, the embedding model's identity, the ID and the version of the default configuration, the service's version and its capabilities bellman-matsya index, bellman-matsya configuration effective POST /v1/search a search: query, and optionally collections, limit, source_ids and boosts; at most 16 KiB index_digest and passages, the passages that best match the query bellman-matsya search POST /v1/answer the body of a search one sentence copied from a matching passage, with its evidence, or none none GET /v1/passages/{passage_id} none; the query parameter index_digest is optional one passage the function passage of the Python module POST /v1/sessions {"name": …}; at most 16 KiB 201 and the new session bellman-matsya session new GET /v1/sessions/{session_id} none the session: its entries, the version of its text, its jobs and its turns bellman-matsya session show POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/entries one entry: text, kind, replies_to, delivery_id; at most 24 MiB the session, with the entry appended bellman-matsya session add POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/selected-job {"job": …}; at most 16 KiB the session bellman-matsya session select POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns a question; at most 256 KiB 202, the turn's identifier, its configuration ID, its credential_source and its route bellman-matsya ask GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/turns/{turn_id} none the turn, with its record once it has finished bellman-matsya ask, while it waits; bellman-matsya turn status, bellman-matsya turn wait POST /v1/model-iterations a job's request; at most 24 MiB 202, the job's identifier and state, its configuration ID, its credential_source and its route, with the fields of §§5 and 6 for a request that names a delivery_id or reviewed_through bellman-matsya job submit, bellman-matsya job submit-prepared GET /v1/model-iterations/{job_id} none; the query parameter view is optional the job, with its record once it has ended bellman-matsya job status, bellman-matsya job wait POST /v1/model-iterations/{job_id}/cancel none the job bellman-matsya job cancel POST /v1/configurations a checked configuration folder as a ZIP archive, Content-Type: application/zip; at most 24 MiB 201 and the configuration's ID and version, or 200 for an ID already published bellman-matsya configuration publish PUT /v1/configurations/default {"configuration_id": …}; at most 16 KiB the former and the new default's ID with the new version bellman-matsya configuration set-default

An answer has the status 200 unless the table names another. The routes of a job, a question and an entry also read the header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key of §1, and no other route reads it. The service also answers GET /healthz with {"status":"ok"}, without a Matsya token; that route serves the administrator's check on the server itself, since the address the administrator gives passes only the routes under /v1/ to the service.

Where the table names a command of matsya-client, the command sends the same request, and its option --json prints the service's answer as it arrived, except that bellman-matsya job submit-prepared and bellman-matsya configuration effective print an object that the client assembles from the answer (The command reference §§4.1 and 9).

docs.title: 3 Refusals
docs.text:
The service answers a refused request with one field, {"detail": "<a sentence>"}, whose sentence states the fault, and one of these statuses:

Status When the service answers it 401 The Authorization header holds no Matsya token, or one that the service does not hold or has revoked. Check the Matsya token the administrator gave you, and ask the administrator if the service refuses it. A request that includes a personal Anthropic key receives the same 401, since the key grants no access of its own. 403 A search or an answer names a collection that your Matsya token is not granted; the sentence is Collection access is not granted (Collections and weights §2). A publication or a change of the default was sent with a Matsya token whose holder the administrator has not named as an administrator (§8). A job, a question or an entry includes the header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key (§1) and is sent to a service whose operator has not enabled personal keys; the sentence is This service does not accept a personal Anthropic key, a request that repeats a delivery_id is refused in the same way, and nothing is created. 404 The session, job, turn or passage does not exist or is not yours; the service does not distinguish the two cases. A passage also receives 404 when your Matsya token may not read its collection, or when the service no longer keeps the version of the index that the request names. A question also receives 404 when the service offers no turns of matsya-master, or when it keeps no version of the index with the digest the question names. A job, a question or a change of the default that names a configuration ID the service has not published receives 404, and no job or question is recorded. 409 A cancellation names a job that has ended; the sentence is The job has ended. A question repeats a delivery_id with another question or another configuration selector than the turn the session holds under it. A job's request repeats a delivery_id under which you hold a job with another request; the sentence is The delivery_id names a job whose request differs (§5). A job's request names in reviewed_through an entry after which the session holds further entries; the sentence names each of them by its number and kind, as in The session holds an entry after entry 1, the last entry the request reviewed: entry 2 (user); review it and submit again (§6). Neither of the last two creates a job. 413 The body exceeds the route's limit (§2), a published archive whose contents expand beyond 24 MiB among them. 415 A body was sent without the header Content-Type: application/json, or a publication without Content-Type: application/zip. 422 The request is malformed: a field that the route does not know, a value outside its range, a view other than products or full, a configuration ID that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, or an entry, a selection or a job that the session cannot hold, such as a reply that names an entry that is not a question. A job's request whose reviewed_through names no entry of the session also receives 422, with a sentence such as The session holds no entry 3; its last entry is entry 2, and no job is created (§6). A question also receives 422 when the configuration it selects, or the default, does not enable the conversation role; no question is appended. A published archive receives 422 when an entry escapes the folder, is a link or is not a regular file, when two entries share a name, when a file is absent from the manifest or differs from its digest, or when the configuration fails any check. The header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key is present with an empty or blank value; the sentence is The Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key header is empty. A reply that would start the next attempt of a job run under a personal Anthropic key includes no such header; the sentence is The job awaiting this reply ran under a personal Anthropic key; send the reply with a personal Anthropic key, and the session is left unchanged (§6). 503 The service cannot read its database of Matsya tokens, or holds no retrieval index. Report the route and the answer to the administrator.

The service answers an empty header with 422, and any other with 403 when its operator has not enabled personal keys, after its check of the Matsya token and before it reads the request's body. None of the three refusals of a personal key uses 401, which concerns the Matsya token alone, and none creates a job, a turn or an entry. When the service refuses a request that a command of matsya-client sent, the command prints the sentence and exits with status 1; for a reply refused for want of a key, it adds a sentence that says how to supply one (§6).

docs.title: 4 The index, a search and a passage
docs.text:
A search sends a query and receives the passages of the index that best match it. Without collections, it searches every collection your Matsya token may read. This example restricts the search to the repository:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/search" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"query": "decision perch state and controls", "collections": ["repository"], "limit": 4}'

The answer is {"index_digest": "…", "passages": [ … ]}, with the passages in the order of their scores, each with its identifier, its source, its location, its text and its scores. Collections and weights gives the fields of the request (§3), how the passages are ranked (§4) and what a passage holds (§5). bellman-matsya search "decision perch state and controls" --collections repository --limit 4 sends the same request.

POST /v1/answer takes the same body and answers with one sentence copied from a retrieved passage whose words match the query's, or with none. No language model is called, and nothing is paraphrased:

{"answer": "…", "method": "extractive", "index_digest": "…", "passage_ids": ["…"],
 "evidence": [{"passage_id": "…", "excerpt": "…", "source_id": "…", "title": "…",
               "path": "…", "location": {"…": "…"}, "authority": "…"}],
 "explanation": "The answer quotes retrieved source text. No model checked the economics."}

When no short sentence matches, answer is null, evidence is empty and the explanation says that no matching excerpt was found. The explanation of a sentence taken from a PDF, or from a transcription or a secondary reading of an article, asks you to compare its claims with the page of the PDF before you accept them.

A passage is read again by its identifier:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/passages/<passage_id>?index_digest=<index_digest>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

Without index_digest, the route reads the index the service reads now. With it, the route reads the version of the index that the digest names, so that a passage cited from an earlier version can be read again, as long as the service keeps that version and your Matsya token may read the passage's collection. The answer is the passage as a search returns it, without the scores.

docs.title: 5 A job
docs.text:
A job's request is one JSON object with a source and, optionally, the fields that shape the job. The roles that the table names are described in The roles and the work of a job §1.

Field What it gives source the source material, in one of two forms: {"kind": "description", "text": "…"}, a model's description in prose and displayed equations, or {"kind": "paper", "text": "…"}, a paper as its text in Markdown or LaTeX; a paper sent as numbered pages or as a PDF is refused with 422 and the sentence A paper is sent as text: source.text holds the paper in Markdown or LaTeX session in place of source, the identifier of a session, whose text the job reads as it stands when the job starts, or as it stood when the service accepted the job where the request names reviewed_through (§6) reviewed_through with session alone, the number of the session's last entry when you reviewed it, an integer from 1: the service checks the session against it and fixes the job's source material when it accepts the job (§6) max_cycles the most iterations after the initial declaration: a positive integer, by default the configuration's cycle limit, three at present, and at most the configuration's maximum, five at present force true sends the job on to writing when preparation, the step of the Model-prose-writer, ends with questions, which then stand in its record; without it, such a job ends needs_input starting_declaration files that the first cycle checks in place of the first writing by Prose-to-Bellman-Sym: an object that maps file names, <name>.bl for a stage file, period.yml, trellis.yml or note.md, to the files' texts; files that the elaborator, the program that checks stage files, refuses go back to Prose-to-Bellman-Sym for repair target required: the level of the declaration the job writes, one of stage, period, trellis and recipe (Matsya in three parts §2 says what each holds); a request without it, or with another word, is refused with target must be stage, period, trellis or recipe formulation a sentence of at most 500 characters that names the one formulation to write, when the source states several model_key, source_cluster two labels in lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, sent together, that name the groups of indexed sources the job must not read (Collections and weights §6) configuration_id the ID of a published configuration the job runs under, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (§8); without it the job runs under the service's default, and the answer names the ID resolved either way delivery_id a name of 1 to 64 characters for the request: the same request sent again under it is answered with the job you hold under it and creates none, whatever has changed since; another request under the same name is refused with 409

A request that holds both source and session, or neither, reviewed_through without session, or a field outside this table, is refused with 422. The source's text, a paper's included, is sent to the language-model provider, so ask the service's administrator before you submit a paper that may not leave your machine. A PDF is converted to Markdown or LaTeX before it is sent.

Write the request into a file, request.json:

{
  "target": "stage",
  "source": {
    "kind": "description",
    "text": "A household lives forever with discount factor beta. It holds cash on hand m. It consumes c in [0, m] and saves a = m - c. Next period m = R a + y, with y iid lognormal, mean one, standard deviation sigma. Utility is CRRA with risk aversion rho. It maximizes expected discounted utility."
  },
  "max_cycles": 1
}

and send it:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @request.json

The answer, with the status 202, gives the job's identifier, the key used for its language-model calls and the route of its record:

{"id":"<job>","state":"queued","configuration_id":"<id>","credential_source":"service","status_url":"/v1/model-iterations/<job>"}

bellman-matsya job submit model.md --target stage --no-session --max-cycles 1 sends the same request for the description kept in the file model.md. Without --no-session, the command first creates a session, appends the file's text to it and starts the job from the session (§6).

A request that names a delivery_id can be sent again when its answer was lost, as when the connection failed after the request was sent. The service answers the same request sent again under the same name with the job you hold under it, its present state in state and "repeated":true, even where the job's session has received entries since, and creates no second job; the answer to a new request that names a delivery_id holds "repeated":false. A different request under a name you have used is refused with 409 and the sentence The delivery_id names a job whose request differs, and nothing is created. This is the capability job_delivery_id of §1.

With a personal Anthropic key (§1), sent only to an HTTPS address or to a service on your own machine, the job's request includes one more header, and the answer names "credential_source":"client"; bellman-matsya job submit adds the header itself when a key is selected:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key: $BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @request.json

The job is read from its route:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations/<job>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

The answer holds the job's state: queued, running, and at its end converged, not_converged, needs_input, cancelled, failed or interrupted. It holds the job's label, whose text names the session, the target, the version of the session's text the job read, the job's number in the session and its state, such as a household · stage · version 1 · job 1 · running, and is the target and the state for a job of no session; cancel_requested, whether you asked to cancel the job; progress, the step the job has reached, preparation, writing, prose_writing or judging, with its cycle (0 for the initial writing); and events, the records of the job's calls of language models, each with the role called, the size and digest of its message, the counts of language-model tokens (Matsya in three parts §1), and any failure, but no text. A job of a session also holds session; once it has started, or from its acceptance for a job whose request named reviewed_through (§6), revision and entry_numbers, the version of the text it read and the numbers of the entries it read; for such a job, reviewed_through, the entry its request named; and at its end current, whether the text stayed at that version while it ran. A job whose request named a delivery_id holds it under delivery_id. A job that matsya-master started at your request names that turn under started_by. Every job holds configuration_id, the ID of the configuration it runs under, fixed when the service accepted it and unchanged by a later change of the default; request_sha256, the digest of the request as accepted, computed over its fields except configuration_id, so that two jobs with equal digests received the same source bytes, target and other fields; source_sha256, the digest of the source text the job reads, fixed at acceptance for a source sent with the request and for a session's text fixed then (§6), and otherwise when the job starts, a description stripped of surrounding whitespace and a paper unchanged; and index_digest, the digest of the index the job selected when it began. Each of the three digests is null until fixed, and all four fields are null for a job recorded before the service kept them. A failed or cancelled job keeps its configuration_id and request_sha256. Every job also holds credential_source, client when its language-model calls are made with the personal Anthropic key sent with its request (§1) and service when they are made with the service's own key, fixed when the service accepted the job and kept when the job fails or is interrupted; a job recorded before the service kept the field reads service, the only key there then was. The field names a key and never holds one; a job that made no call caused no charge to either account; and neither configuration_id nor request_sha256 depends on it.

A job runs for minutes. Read its route again every half minute until its state is neither queued nor running; bellman-matsya job wait <job> does this and prints each new step. In a shell without Python, this loop waits and then prints the job:

JOB="<job>"
while curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations/$JOB" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" | grep -Eq '"state": *"(queued|running)"'; do
  sleep 30
done
curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations/$JOB" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

Once the job has ended, its record stands under result, in one of two views, which the query parameter view selects. The default view, products, gives the products of the job and the material of its report:

  • status and reason, the outcome and why the job stopped, such as semantic_fixed_point, cycle_limit_reached or token_ceiling_reached;
  • schema, the form of the record; description, the prepared model prose, and questions;
  • paper_source_check, the reports of the prose-source-judge, and paper_form_check, the check of the model prose's headings and length;
  • available_writing, the latest nonempty parsed declaration files, giving their cycle number, the files and the prose from which they were written as description, or null if no writing produced parsed files; cycle 0 is the initial declaration, and a not_converged job may still return its files for review;
  • cycles_run, the number of iterations after the initial declaration, and last_cycle: under files the stage files of the actual last iteration, which may be empty even when available_writing holds earlier files; under judging the reports of the prose-roundtrip-judge, under comparison whether adjacent elaborated semantic objects are equivalent (equal) and their first difference, under citations_supported whether every block quotes the prose from which that declaration was written, and under unresolved_note whether note.md leaves something open;
  • last_completed_comparison, the latest completed comparison with its left and right cycle numbers (0 names the initial elaborated object), its equal verdict and first difference; it is null if no comparison completed, even if a later iteration began;
  • reading, the digests of the index read and of the reference guides given to the roles;
  • captured_source, for a job whose request named reviewed_through, the history it was built from: reviewed_through, revision and entries, the numbers of the entries it read (§6);
  • usage, the language-model tokens charged to each role and to the job, the number of calls of each role, and the refusal, when a ceiling refused a call.

The roles and the two kinds of prose are described in The roles and the work of a job §1. The view full gives the complete record: initial_writing, the first declaration from the prepared prose, then every numbered iteration with its prose writing, declaration writing, judging and adjacent comparison; every call; the record of what each role read; continues, the earlier job of the same session that this job continues, by its identifier, its status and the digest of its source, or null, fixed at acceptance for a job whose request named reviewed_through (§6); the versions of the program and of the configuration; and, for a converged job, artifacts, the files of a model folder:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations/<job>?view=full" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

bellman-matsya job status <job> reads the default view, and bellman-matsya job files <job> <folder> --all-iterates reads the full view as well. A not_converged job with a record can be read and written to a folder in the same way as a converged job; its report states why the checks did not conclude. A failed job holds no record, and its error names a fixed code: for instance provider_error; incomplete_model_response, an answer cut off before it could be parsed into files; prompt_too_long, a message longer than its role's limit or the language model's context window; provider_rejected_request, a message that the language-model provider rejected without processing it; provider_rejected_credential, an Anthropic API key that Anthropic refused, after its first such answer and with no request under another key, where the job's credential_source names the key refused: replace your key, or stop sending it, when it is client, and tell the administrator when it is service; invalid_request, a source the service could not read; or configuration_refused, with the part refused under error_detail. A job that a restart of the service interrupted holds the code server_restarted.

A converged job has a pair of adjacent elaborated semantic objects that the comparator found equivalent. The prose judges, the check of quotations in the stage files and the writer's note are reported separately; they do not decide convergence. If an iteration's declaration cannot be elaborated, that iteration has no comparison verdict. Read the diagnostics to assess whether the prepared prose and the declaration state the model you meant. Older records can retain the earlier success reasons semantic_fixed_point_and_declaration_checks or source_agreement_and_semantic_fixed_point; those names describe the stopping rule in force when the jobs ran. The files remain proposals: the service writes nothing on your machine, and bellman-matsya job files writes them only into the folder you name. Keep a job's identifier with its result, since the administrator needs it to trace a failure or an unexpected answer.

A queued or running job is cancelled through its route cancel, with no body:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations/<job>/cancel" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

A queued job ends cancelled at once and never runs. A running job is marked cancel_requested and stops before its next call to the language-model provider: a call already sent finishes and is charged, and the job then ends cancelled, keeping its record with the usage of the calls it made. The answer is the job as its route gives it. A job that has ended cannot be cancelled: the service answers 409 with {"detail":"The job has ended"}. bellman-matsya job cancel <job> sends the same request.

docs.title: 6 Sessions, entries and the selected job
docs.text:
A session is created with its name, a text of at most 200 characters:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"name": "a household"}'

The answer, with the status 201, is the session as its route gives it: its id and name; entries, its numbered entries; revision, the version of its text, which is the number of its last entry of the kind user, paper or acceptance; awaiting_answer, the job whose questions await your reply, or null; selected_job; jobs, each with its id, state, revision, current and label, in the order they were created; and turns, the identifiers of the turns asked in it. bellman-matsya session new "a household" sends the same request. The session is read from its route, as bellman-matsya session show <session> reads it:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions/<session>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

An entry is appended with its text:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions/<session>/entries" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"text": "A household saves out of cash on hand and faces a risky income."}'

The body holds text; kind, which is user by default, paper for the text of a paper, or acceptance; replies_to, the number of the entry it answers; and delivery_id, a name of 1 to 64 characters, with which a repeated request returns the entry already stored and appends nothing. A reply, of the kind user or paper, names a question of Matsya in replies_to. An acceptance holds no text and names in replies_to the answer of matsya-master it accepts; only an accepted answer enters the text that a later job reads. A reply of the kind user to a question of the job that the session awaits starts that job's next attempt at once; the attempt reads the session's text as it stands when it starts, the reply included, even where the job it continues was fixed at acceptance.

Such a reply may include the header Bellman-Matsya-Anthropic-Key (§1); the attempt it starts then uses that key and records credential_source client, and a reply without the header starts the attempt under the service's key. The service keeps no key, so a job that ran under a personal key, with credential_source client, is continued only by a reply that includes a key again: a reply to it without the header is refused with 422 and the sentence The job awaiting this reply ran under a personal Anthropic key; send the reply with a personal Anthropic key, and the session's entries, its awaiting mark and its jobs stay as they were. The key may differ from the one the earlier job used, and a reply to a job that ran under the service's key may include a key for the next attempt. A request that repeats a delivery_id starts no work and needs no key.

The answer is the session with three more fields: entry, the entry as stored, with its number, kind, text, origin, replies_to and the time it was appended, where origin names the job or the turn that wrote an entry of Matsya and is null for yours; repeated; and scheduled, the identifier, the route and the credential_source of the job that a reply started, or null. bellman-matsya session add <session> notes.md sends the same request, with --kind, --replies-to and --delivery-id for the other fields. With --replies-to, an entry of the kind user is sent with a selected key in the header, and for a reply that the service refuses for want of a key the command adds to the service's sentence Supply one with bellman-matsya configure --set-anthropic-key, BELLMAN_MATSYA_ANTHROPIC_KEY, or MatsyaClient(..., anthropic_api_key=...).

A job is started from the session's text by naming the session in place of a source:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"session": "<session>", "target": "stage"}'

Such a job reads the session's entries up to the version of the text at the moment it starts, an answer of matsya-master among them only when you have accepted it, so that it also reads an entry appended while it waits to start; a session that holds no text is refused with 422. bellman-matsya job submit --session <session> sends the same request.

A job's request may also name reviewed_through, the number of the session's last entry when you reviewed it, so that the job reads the text you reviewed and no later one:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/model-iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"session": "<session>", "target": "stage", "reviewed_through": 2, "delivery_id": "a-household-stage-1"}'

The service checks the session against that number in the step in which it accepts the job. A session that holds an entry after it is refused with 409 and a sentence that names each such entry by its number and kind, such as The session holds an entry after entry 1, the last entry the request reviewed: entry 2 (user); review it and submit again, and a number beyond the session's last entry with 422 and a sentence such as The session holds no entry 3; its last entry is entry 2; neither creates a job, and you submit again once you have read the later entries. Otherwise the service fixes the job's source material at acceptance: in the same step it records the session's text as it then stands, an answer of matsya-master among its entries only when you have accepted it, the version of that text, the numbers of its entries, and the earlier job that the new one continues, the session's latest job that holds a record and was current at its end. The job reads these when it starts, in place of the session, so that neither an entry appended nor a job ended while it waits changes what it reads. The answer, with the status 202, adds reviewed_through, revision and entry_numbers to the fields of §5, the job's route holds them from then on, and the job's record names the history it was built from under captured_source, as {"reviewed_through": 2, "revision": 2, "entries": [1, 2]} for a session of two entries of the kind user. This is the capability capture_at_acceptance of §1. bellman-matsya job submit-prepared <file> sends such a request from a prepared-inputs file, after it has checked that the service names the capability (The command reference §4.1).

The selected job (Matsya in three parts §3) is set through the route selected-job: the selection names a job of the session that holds a record, and null clears it:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions/<session>/selected-job" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"job": "<job>"}'

The answer is the session. A job of another session, or one that holds no record, is refused with 422. bellman-matsya session select <session> <job> sends the same request, and bellman-matsya session select <session> --none sends {"job": null}.

docs.title: 7 A question in a session
docs.text:
A question is asked in a session and answered in a turn of matsya-master:

curl --fail-with-body -sS -X POST "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions/<session>/turns" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"question": "What does the decision perch of a stage hold?"}'

The body is one JSON object of at most 256 KiB. It holds question, of at most 8,000 characters, and optionally:

  • stage_file, the text of one stage file, which the service elaborates so that the language model reads its dossier (The roles and the work of a job §1) and never the file's text;
  • refusal, timing and package_version, material of your own: the elaborator's refusal of a file of yours, the timing of your model and the version of the bellman package you use (at most 200 characters), each placed in the language model's message under its name;
  • index_digest, the digest of an earlier version of the index to read, as an earlier turn's record names it;
  • delivery_id, a name of 1 to 64 characters, with which a repeated request returns the turn already asked; a repeated name with another question or another configuration_id is refused with 409;
  • configuration_id, the ID of a published configuration whose conversation role answers (§8); without it the default answers. A configuration that does not enable the role refuses the question with 422 before anything is appended.

The question is appended to the session as an entry, and the answer, with the status 202, is

{"id":"<turn>","state":"queued","question":4,"repeated":false,"configuration_id":"<id>","credential_source":"service","status_url":"/v1/sessions/<session>/turns/<turn>"}

where question is the number of your question's entry, and credential_source is client when the question was sent with a personal Anthropic key (§1) and service otherwise. The turn is read from its route:

curl --fail-with-body -sS "$BELLMAN_MATSYA_SERVER/v1/sessions/<session>/turns/<turn>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BELLMAN_MATSYA_TOKEN"

Its state is queued or running, and at its end finished, failed or interrupted; a turn takes about a minute, so read the route again every ten seconds until it has ended. A finished turn holds its record, whose result gives:

  • status: answered; needs_input, with Matsya's questions in questions; or incomplete, with the reason in reason and an answer of two fixed sentences, for instance when the requests for further material allowed in one turn were used up or a call would have passed the turn's ceiling of language-model tokens. When Anthropic refused the Anthropic API key of the turn's calls, after its first such answer and with no request under another key, the reason is provider_rejected_credential and the answer is the one sentence Matsya could not answer, because the language-model provider refused the Anthropic API key used for this turn.;
  • answer and citations, each citation with the quoted sentence, the identity, path, heading and location of the material it quotes, and the digest of the index read;
  • passages, the material given to the language model, by identity, path and location;
  • job, the job whose outputs the turn read, by its identifier and label, or null;
  • job_started, the job that the turn started when you asked for one, by its identifier and label, or null;
  • current, whether you added no entry to the session while the question was answered.

The record's usage gives the language-model tokens charged in the turn, by role and in total, and the ceilings in force. The turn's answer holds configuration_id, the ID pinned to it; a job the turn starts at your request runs under that same ID. It also holds credential_source, kept when the turn fails or is interrupted, and a job the turn starts at your request uses the turn's key, so that the job of a turn asked with a personal key has credential_source client too. A failed turn names under error the code configuration_refused, processing_failed or worker_unavailable, and a turn that a restart of the service interrupted names server_restarted. The answer, or Matsya's questions, are appended to the session as entries of the kind answer or question that reply to your question's entry. bellman-matsya ask <session> "<question>" sends the same question, waits for the turn and prints the answer; its options --stage-file, --index-digest, --delivery-id and --configuration-id send the fields of those names, and a selected personal key is sent in the header of §1. With --no-wait, the command prints the turn's identifier as soon as the service has accepted the question and does not wait for the answer; bellman-matsya turn status <session> <turn> then reads the turn's route once, and bellman-matsya turn wait <session> <turn> reads it until the turn has ended, from the same terminal or another.

docs.title: 8 Publishing and selecting configurations
docs.text:
A configuration is the checked folder of instruction texts, settings, Matsya handlers and saved guides that a job or a turn runs under (Matsya developer guide §1). Its configuration ID is the SHA-256 digest of its manifest.json, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The service keeps every published configuration unchanged under its ID and one default, which a request that names no ID runs under. A configuration ID selects a configuration; it is not a Matsya token, and any valid Matsya token may select any published ID. Publishing a configuration and changing the default are reserved for the administrators the service's operator names, since a configuration holds Python code the service runs.

An administrator publishes a checked folder by sending it as a ZIP archive whose entries are the folder's files by their paths relative to the folder:

(cd candidate && zip -r -q - .) > candidate.zip
