1. Open the stage file in Files, or double-click the stage at the period you want to inspect in Trellis. Once saved, the revised equation applies at every occurrence that uses the same file.
  2. Select the relevant box in the stage graph, then choose its source link in Details to open the defining line in the editor.
  3. Edit the equation in the editor. If it now reads or writes a different field, check its declaration and the block’s header, which lists the fields the block reads or writes. Field equations describes the syntax.

For example, the consumption and savings stage defines saving by a = m_d - c, where m_d is cash on hand at the decision and c is consumption. After changing that budget equation, use Initial to check the fields it reads and writes, then trace where saving is used in the model graph.

docs.title: 2 Check the graph after editing
docs.text:
Pause after typing to let Workbench read the new text. When the reading succeeds, the graph updates from the editor. If the text is refused, the editor marks the line and Problems lists the reason. When a previous graph is available, Workbench dims it and labels it last constructed. Use the marked source line to correct the current text.

A stage can construct in one direction and have a refused graph in the other. Check Forward and Backward when an equation affects both. Construction and binding let you inspect the equations and their supplied values and methods. Computing a numerical policy or simulating the model requires a separate step.

docs.title: 3 Edit field declarations
docs.text:
In Inspector → Fields, choose the table for arrival, decision, or continuation. Select a field name to find its declaration. Where a set or role is editable, enter the new set or choose a role. To add a field, complete New field and Set, choose its role, then select +. In a branching stage, use the table for the branch you intend to change.

These actions edit the source in the editor. Check Problems, then save the file to keep the change. See Stage fields for the declaration rules.

docs.title: 4 Change parameter values and methods
docs.text:
Open the stage as an occurrence of the recipe you intend to change. In Inspector, use the relevant tab to find the source for that occurrence.

Tab What you can edit Parameters Enter a value in an editable row and press Enter. The source is a calibration file. The stage’s declaration gives the parameter’s allowed set. Settings Enter a value of the kind the settings file expects and press Enter. For example, keep an integer setting as an integer. Methods Where a YAML entry has a picker, choose a method from the choices admitted for that computation. Open the methods file in the editor to change options such as a grid.

Confirming a row writes its source file without pressing Save in the editor. Save or discard any unsaved edits to that file before using the row. If the tab names no source, open the recipe and use its Recipe tab or edit its text to attach the appropriate file. Model directory layout · Methodization

A .bl file whose first nonblank line is @methods: followed by the stage name is a methods addition. Workbench opens it as text and lists additions kept beside their stage files in the Recipe tab’s methods choices. When the recipe selects an addition, the package reads it with the stage. The Methods tab displays any methods it binds as text. To change the addition, edit and save the file itself. Matsya’s Build declaration refuses a model whose selected files include a methods addition.

To trace an executable routine, follow the method's source link in Methods and check the handler named there. A tag displayed in the graph identifies the bound method. The method file or addition gives the declaration you need to trace its implementation.

docs.title: 5 Undo and save
docs.text:
Use Command+Z on macOS or Ctrl+Z on Windows and Linux to undo an edit in the editor. If you made an unsaved change through the graph, undo it from the editor tab of a file that the change edited.

Choose Save to write the open editor tab. If an edit changed several files, save each tab marked unsaved. For a value already written through an Inspector row, restore the earlier value in its source file.

docs.title: Create and connect stages
docs.text: A trellis is the model's arrangement of stages across periods. A stage occurrence is one use of a stage in one period. To connect two occurrences, pair a continuation state field of the writing stage with an arrival state field of the reading stage. The stage defines the equations. The connector identifies which state field supplies which.

docs.title: 1 Create the model folder
docs.text:
1. Save any unsaved work before switching folders. In Files, choose New trellis. Enter a Name, the number of Periods, and a Parent folder outside any existing model folder. The form shows the destination. Period label (optional) names the repeated period.
  2. Under Templates, choose the stages to start with. Each chosen stage has a key, the name used in the recipe and period lists. Keep Every period for a repeated stage or choose Terminal period for a stage such as a bequest. When using templates in a model with several periods, keep at least one stage on Every period. For an empty model folder, leave the templates unselected.
  3. Choose Write the folder. The Workbench opens declaration/spec.yml in the new folder. The recipe names the trellis and its stage files. The trellis lists its periods and starts with empty connector mappings for you to fill. If you chose templates, their files are copied into the folder.

See Model directory layout for the files that make up a model.

docs.title: 2 Write or reuse a stage
docs.text:
Write a stage from scratch. With a recipe in the model folder, choose New stage in Files, enter a unique Stage key, and choose Write the stage. Save pending edits to the recipe or the checklist file answers.yml first if the form names them. The Workbench opens declaration/stages/<key>/<key>.bl, with starter block headers, and saves its row in the active recipe. Declare the fields and equations in the stage file. Add its key to the intended period's stages list to give it an occurrence. If the graph or the Recipe table is unavailable during this step, edit that list in the period or trellis file directly. A recipe and the periods it names must agree on the stage keys. Periods written out and repeated.

Place an existing stage or copy a template.

  1. Open Trellis, set Graph to Operator, and set Direction to Forward. Open the target period and choose + Stage, then choose an item from the list. You can also open Stages above the graph and drag an item onto the period. With the recipe open, Stage under the Inspector's Recipe table offers the same choices, with Period file where there is more than one template.
  2. Choose a stage already in the folder to list it in the period, or choose a template to copy its declaration and companion files and add a recipe row. If the template's key is taken, enter another key in Add stage and choose Add the stage. The library section shows reusable stages from your configured library. Choose from a folder… to copy from a stage folder or a .bl file on disk. A trellis that lists its stages directly as records offers stages from the current folder.
  3. Check the status line for the affected periods. Several periods can share the same stage list, so adding a stage to that list can place it in all of them. Check the new card for unjoined fields and add the intended connections.

The Workbench reads a stage library from BELLMAN_STAGE_LIBRARY, a list of local folder paths separated by the operating system's path separator, or from ~/.bellman/library/ by default. The copy in the model is a separate file from the library stage.

docs.title: 3 Add a period
docs.text:
1. In Trellis → Operator → Forward, choose + Period before the earliest period or between two periods. If the target period is outside the current range, select all in the period selector, then Fit. Open a collapsed period with its chevron. You can also drop a stage from Stages on that control to select it for the new period.
  2. In Add period, enter a Label, choose at least one stage, and select Add the period. The form writes declaration/period.<label>.yml immediately. It adds the reference to the trellis in the editor. Save that tab to keep the reference. In a trellis that lists stage records directly, the control inserts a period with the neighbouring period's stages.
  3. Inspect the new joins. Inserting between two periods increases the indices of periods on the earlier side and adjusts the recipe's corresponding ranges. Check any age or calibration schedule keyed by period index. To add a period after the terminal period, edit the trellis file directly. Trellis syntax and period numbering.

docs.title: 4 Connect two stages
docs.text:
1. In Trellis → Operator → Forward, show both occurrences. To add a connection, drag an unused continuation plug of the writing stage to the arrival socket of a different stage in the same period or the next period in economic time. The terminal period is periods[0], so a connection from periods[1] to periods[0] goes forward.
  2. In Join, check the proposed field pairs and their declared sets. Choose the missing pairs and tick the ones you want to write. The Workbench proposes equal-name matches where the model can infer them. Join writes the ticked pairs into the period's connectors or the trellis's inter_connectors. When working with individual field ports, a direct drag can write one pair.
  3. Select the resulting cable, the line connecting the occurrences, and read Details. It shows the field pairs, their declared sets, their origin, and the source of authored pairs. Check every period or pair of periods that uses the same mapping before saving it.

For a branch-specific example, work in a copy of Retirement Choice. Add an earlier period with ret_choice and worker_cons as in §3, then place the existing retiree_cons in that period as in §2. Drag the retire plug of ret_choice to retiree_cons in the new period. In the row for arrival field a_ret, choose continuation field a_r, then select Join. Details identifies the retire route and the written pair. Check the new retiree stage's inter-period connections separately.

The gesture needs a connectors list for a join within a period or an inter_connectors mapping for a join between periods. If the relevant entry is missing, add a place for the pairs in the source first. The language reference shows how to write an empty mapping and how a single inter-period mapping applies to repeated period pairs. Connectors within a period and Inter-period connectors.

An incomplete pairing can write the ticked pairs as a draft. Problems identifies the route and the fields still needed for a complete connection. For a refused edit, follow the source link in Problems. If take the line out is offered, it restores the previous text while the file still holds the edit. When a refusal prevents the graph from being rebuilt, the previous graph stays dimmed.

docs.title: 5 Change, remove, and save a connection
docs.text:
• Select a cable and drag a highlighted end to the new stage. If Join opens, check which pairs the move removes and which it writes. A move can replace an inferred match with an authored pair.
  • To remove an authored connection, select its cable and choose Remove in Details, or press Backspace or Delete with focus on the forward graph. If Details says joined by the names, the connection has no authored entry. Use Rename there to change the arrival field's name, or move the join to write an explicit replacement.
  • Inspect the edited source line and the affected periods before saving. Command+Z on macOS or Ctrl+Z on Windows and Linux reverses the latest edit in the editor. For a graph gesture that changes several files, undo from one of the affected tabs while the files still hold the gesture's edits. Save writes the open file. Open and save each file marked unsaved to keep the whole change. New stage and period files created by placement are already on disk.
  • After undo, let the graph finish updating before dragging the same connection again.

docs.title: 6 Remove a stage or period
docs.text:
Select a stage card in the forward trellis. In Details, Remove from periods … removes the stage from the period list shown. A shared period file can affect several occurrences. Remove stage removes it from the active recipe and the periods that use it. To remove a period, select its frame and choose Remove period where offered. Check the affected files, mappings and period ranges in the status line.

Workbench marks unused files deleted on save when a removal would leave them without a reference. Review those marks before saving. Use Keep to withdraw a file removal offered in Files, or undo the model edit before saving. A file that another recipe still uses stays in the project.

docs.title: Manage recipes and variants
docs.text: A recipe names the trellis file, the stage declarations, and the sources that supply parameter values, numerical settings, and method assignments. Each use of a stage in a period is a stage occurrence, with the sources the recipe selects for that period. The base recipe is declaration/spec.yml. The Bellman factory.

docs.title: 1 Select a recipe and inspect a stage
docs.text:
1. Open the model folder containing declaration/. In Files, choose spec.yml or a variant such as spec.high-risk.yml. The editor opens the file, Trellis shows that recipe's periods, and the path at the top names the active recipe.
  2. Open Inspector to see Recipe under the editor. The top control names the trellis file. Each stage row shows the stage key, its file, and entries under Calibration, Settings, Methods, and Periods.
  3. To see the values used at a particular occurrence, double-click its card in Trellis, or select the card and choose Open the stage in Details. The stage file opens with that occurrence's bindings. Use Parameters, Settings, or Methods in the Inspector. The position control in the top path lets you select another occurrence when the file is used more than once. If opening a stage from Files shows it without values, select the intended recipe and open the stage from its trellis card.

The period selector above the graph filters what you see. Choose all or a period range, untick stage keys to hide their occurrences, or type a restriction such as periods 0–2, stages cons, port, or periods 0–1, stages cons and press Enter. The restriction affects the view. To change the periods in which a stage occurs, edit its recipe row as described below.

docs.title: 2 Change the files a recipe uses
docs.text:
1. Open the recipe and click a stage row in Recipe, or focus the row and press Enter or Space. The open row shows selectors for its stage file and its existing source entries. Use the trellis selector above the table to choose a different trellis file.
  2. Choose a file of the matching kind. Calibration supplies parameter values, Settings supplies numerical choices such as grid sizes, and Methods names the routines attached to named targets in the stage. A source list is read in order, with later entries overriding assignments to the same name. Sources listed for a period range apply after the common all list. To add a source entry or range list, edit the recipe text.
  3. An entry such as $cons_calibration is a slot, a place for a mapping passed when loading the recipe in Python. An unfilled slot contributes no assignments. To use a saved source in the Workbench, replace the slot with a matching file in the selector. Where New file is offered beside a slot, it creates a starter source, replaces the slot with its path, and opens the file for editing.
  4. To restrict a stage to certain periods, enter a range such as 0–0 in its Periods cell and press Enter. This writes periods: [0, 0] and leaves the stage active only in the terminal period if the period lists it. Clearing the cell removes the recipe's restriction. This is separate from a source range, which changes the assignments a stage receives in periods where it is already active.
  5. Inspect the recipe's edited text and save it. If New file opened a source, fill and save that file, then return to the recipe and save its changed reference. Reopen an occurrence to check the applied bindings. Problems links to any binding refusal and the source it names.

See Source order, slots and period ranges for the rules on merging sources.

docs.title: 3 Create a variant
docs.text:
1. In Files, choose New variant. It starts from declaration/spec.yml, even if another recipe is open. Save pending changes to the recipe, its trellis file, or a period template it uses before copying.
  2. Enter a Name such as high-risk, using letters, digits, and hyphens, and choose Write the variant. The Workbench creates spec.high-risk.yml, trellis.high-risk.yml, and copies of the period templates the base trellis names. It opens the new recipe and shows its trellis.
  3. Edit period lists or connectors through the variant's files. To vary a calibration, setting, or method independently, give the variant its own source file and choose that file in the variant recipe. To vary an equation, copy the stage declaration to a separate stage folder and point the variant's stage row to it.

The copy shares the original stage files and the calibration, settings, methods, and registry sources they reference until you change those paths. Editing a shared source affects every recipe that names it. The New variant form lists the registry sources the copy keeps, such as an age schedule. Check those sources if the variant changes the periods they describe. Variants in the model directory.

docs.title: 4 Give a variant its own calibration
docs.text:
Change the safe return in a disposable copy of applications/cons-port:

  1. Before opening the copy, duplicate declaration/spec.cons-port.yml as declaration/spec.yml. This gives New variant the base recipe it expects.
  2. Open the copy and create a variant named higher-safe-return. With your file manager or editor, copy declaration/calibration/portfolio.yml to declaration/calibration/portfolio-high.yml. Save any Workbench edits before reloading or reopening the project to list the new file.
  3. Open spec.higher-safe-return.yml. In Recipe, expand the port row and select portfolio-high under Calibration. Check the new path in the recipe, then save it.
  4. Open period 2’s port card from the variant’s trellis. In Parameters, check that the source is portfolio-high.yml, then enter 1.03 for R and press Enter.
  5. Reopen the base recipe and the same period’s port card. Verify that the base still uses portfolio.yml and R = 1.02. To export the comparison, reopen each saved occurrence and keep the export sets separately. Compare solved portfolio choices in your numerical workflow.

docs.title: Share a project and get help
docs.text: Share the model files and the recipe your colleague should open. Add the commit identifier when the files are in Git, and include an exported view when the diagram itself matters.

docs.title: 1 Review and commit changes
docs.text:
In a folder under Git, Workbench shows Git's change marks beside files and offers commit and push under More at the bottom of the window.

If you create a Git repository outside Workbench, close the model window and open it again. In the browser version, stop and restart the Workbench command for that folder.

  1. Save the files you intend to share. Review their changes in your Git client, including any new files.
  2. Open More → commit. Check the branch shown in the form and untick any file you want to leave out. The form lists new, changed and deleted files from the open model folder.
  3. Enter a Message, then choose Commit. The commit records the selected files as saved on disk. Other files previously staged in Git stay staged.
  4. To send the branch to its configured remote, choose push. Workbench uses the credentials available to Git. Check the status line for Git's response.

The commit is local until it is shared. If Git refuses a push, open Problems for its message. Set up the destination or credentials in your usual Git client, then retry. Workbench reference

docs.title: 2 Export a diagram
docs.text:
1. Open the stage or trellis you want to share. After a change to a bound input, reopen the saved occurrence and check the value before exporting.
  2. Choose More → export view. The status line names the export record under model-explorer/.
  3. Share the .graph.json, .edge-overlays.json and .export.json files together. The record identifies the source files and their fingerprints, the installed Bellman and Workbench versions, and the Git commit when there is one. Workbench keeps these exports outside Git by default. Share them alongside the revision.

For a trellis, the export contains all periods. The record also identifies any restriction applied to the view in Workbench. Save and commit the model first if you want an export tied to a reproducible revision. The export record marks inputs read from unsaved or uncommitted work.

For a paper figure, select a box in a saved stage and choose Paper when offered. Workbench creates a Markdown description and an SVG drawing under paper/. Workbench reference

If you need two exports for a comparison, copy the complete first set to a separate location before exporting the second. A later export can reuse the same filenames.

docs.title: 3 Start an inspection notebook
docs.text:
With a recipe or trellis selected, choose Notebook in Files. Workbench creates notebooks/<folder>.ipynb and names it in the status line. Open it in Jupyter to inspect the saved model. Its cells read the selected recipe or trellis, list the stage occurrences and methods, and record the input fingerprints when you run them.

Keep and edit the notebook in your project. Workbench leaves an existing notebook in place. Use your numerical workflow for the solution.

docs.title: 4 Hand the model to a colleague
docs.text:
Send the whole model folder or the repository revision. Name the recipe to open, such as declaration/spec.yml or a named variant. Keep the files the recipe reads at their relative paths. Include any dependencies it reads outside the model folder. Model directory layout

If you generated files with Matsya, review them and adopt the intended declaration before committing it. Share the economic assumptions and any notebook used for numerical results alongside the declaration. Building a model with Matsya

docs.title: 5 Find and resolve a problem
docs.text:
What you see What to do The desktop app cannot start Workbench. Read the error and its log path. Use Settings → Workbench command… to select the installed executable, then reopen the project. The browser cannot open Workbench. Check the terminal that started it. If its port is occupied, start it with an available port, for example bellman-workbench . --port 8766. The page says No stage file. Open the model folder that contains your declaration. If you are starting from an empty folder, begin with a model description or create a trellis. A diagram is dimmed or a file has an orange error mark. Open Problems and follow the source link. Workbench keeps the previous diagram while the new text has an error. A save reports that the file changed on disk. Choose Compare, then choose which version to keep. Open and edit a project Git refuses a commit or push. Read Git's message in Problems. Resolve the reported issue in Git before retrying.

When reporting a problem, include the Workbench version, the file and line if shown, and the exact diagnostic. For a startup failure, include the relevant part of the log. Installation troubleshooting
